It's also interesting to note that in the rooms on the side of the main hall there are helmet racks, which appear to have helmets on them that look suspiciously like White Knight helmets. Although the base is said to be in Taverley by Solus Dellagar, it is actually underneath the Crafting Guild.

To access the base, the player must enter the trapdoor south of Taverley and run past numerous monsters including chaos dwarves and hill giants. Because of this, it is advised that lower levelled players take food. The base plays a part in the Wanted! quest, where the player must interrogate Lord Daquarius about the whereabouts of Solus Dellagar.

label: Black Knights' Fortress
title: Black Knights' Fortress
lead: The Black Knights are up to no good. You are hired by the white knights to spy on them and destroy their secret weapon.

label: Black Knights' Fortress (location)
title: Black Knights' Fortress (location)
lead:
The Black Knights' Fortress is a castle of the Zamorakian military order of the Kinshra, commonly referred to as the black knights. It plays a central role in the eponymous Black Knights' Fortress quest, and is also visited during the King's Ransom and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

Players attempting to enter the fortress normally will be stopped from doing so by one of the fortress guards. In order to infiltrate the fortress, the player must be wearing one of the following combinations of armour:
*A bronze med helm and an iron chainbody
*A black full helm, black platebody, and black platelegs/black plateskirt
**Black trimmed armour and Black gold-trimmed armour work, as well.
*A set of elite black armour
*The Dark Squall robes

label: Black longsword
title: Black longsword
lead:
The black longsword is a longsword stronger than the steel longsword, but weaker than the mithril longsword. Like all other black weapons, it requires 10 Attack to wield, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can purchase this longsword from the Varrock Swordshop in Varrock.

The black longsword and the steel longsword have the same strength bonus. Black longswords have the same bonuses as a white longsword, other than the +1 prayer bonus the latter offers.

label: Black mace
title: Black mace
lead:
A black mace is a melee weapon stronger than the steel mace, requiring 10 Attack to wield. It is only obtainable in free-to-play by killing dark warriors, from beginner clue scrolls or from Camdozaal Vault lockboxes. Members can also loot it from bronze chests in the Shade Catacombs in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame or from level 106 Cyclops in the Warriors' Guild basement.

As with most maces, it has a Prayer bonus and like all black equipment it cannot be made from raw materials with Smithing.

label: Black med helm
title: Black med helm
lead: A black med helm is the sixth-strongest med helm. It requires a Defence level of 10 to wear, and can be purchased from Seddu's Adventurers' Store in Nardah for 576 coins. It can be received as an uncommon drop from dark warriors, and a common drop from mutated bloodvelds. It can also be obtained through shade burning, and is quite commonly found at the Digsite.

label: Black necklace (interface item)
title: Black necklace (interface item)
lead: The Black necklace is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a necklace, the black necklace appears in its place as a greyed out version.

label: Black platebody
title: Black platebody
lead:
The black platebody is an armour used in melee with the same stat bonuses as a white platebody, excluding the Prayer bonus. It requires 10 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a black chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

It cannot be made using the Smithing skill, though it's easily obtainable as it can be bought from Horvik, Zenesha or another player.

label: Black platebody (g)
title: Black platebody (g)
lead: Black platebody (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black platebody, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platebody (t)
title: Black platebody (t)
lead: Black platebody (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black platebody, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platelegs
title: Black platelegs
lead:
Black platelegs have the same bonuses as the black plateskirt but weigh more. They require level 10 Defence to wear. They can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid or the Champions' Guild. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

Black platelegs are used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if you're part of the Black Arm Gang.

label: Black platelegs (g)
title: Black platelegs (g)
lead: Black platelegs (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Black platelegs, and require level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platelegs (t)
title: Black platelegs (t)
lead: Black platelegs (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Black platelegs, and require level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black plateskirt
title: Black plateskirt
lead:
The black plateskirt has the same stats as black platelegs but weighs less. The black plateskirt requires 10 Defence to wear. One can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

As with all black and white equipment, the black plateskirt cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: Black ring (interface item)
title: Black ring (interface item)
lead: The Black ring is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a ring, the black ring appears in its place as a greyed out version.

label: Black robe
title: Black robe
lead:
A Black robe is one of the basic pieces of chest armour for low level Magic users. Black robes are often dropped by the dark wizards in the stone circle south of Varrock. It has identical stats to the blue wizard robe, as well as its trimmed and gold-trimmed versions. It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard robe; similarly, it can also be turned into a blue wizard robe by using blue dye on it.

The black robe is often worn with the black wizard hat and black skirt for aesthetics. The hat has a slightly darker tone than the robes, instead more closely matching the priest gown. This is not the case with the robe's trimmed versions.

label: Black scimitar
title: Black scimitar
lead:
The black scimitar is a scimitar with a slightly higher attack bonus than the steel scimitar. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

A black scimitar can be found in King Lathas' castle in East Ardougne. The respawn rate of a black scimitar here is about 12 minutes and 30 seconds. It requires level 61 Thieving to access. It can also be bought from Briget's Weapons.

label: Black skirt
title: Black skirt
lead:
Black skirts are one of several skirts available. They are sold by various clothes shops, including Thessalia's shop, Thessalia's Fine Clothes, located in Varrock. They can also be dropped by Forgotten Souls.

Black robe skirts are often worn with black robe tops, in the same way blue skirts are worn with wizard tops. However, they provide no bonuses.

label: Black sq shield
title: Black sq shield
lead: The black square shield (abbreviated in-game as black sq shield) is a square shield made of black metal requiring 10 Defence to equip. Its defensive bonuses are slightly better than those of a steel kiteshield, but slightly inferior to those of a black kiteshield. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

label: Black sword
title: Black sword
lead:
The black sword is a low-mid level weapon made of black, which is stronger than steel. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

As with all black equipment, it offers the same bonuses as white equipment, minus the prayer bonus. Similarly, it cannot be smithed using the Smithing skill.

label: Black toy horsey
title: Black toy horsey
lead:
Black toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says

label: black unicorn
title: black unicorn
lead: The black unicorn is a slightly more dangerous version of the unicorn. These creatures are aggressive to all level players when in the Wilderness, but are low-levelled, so they won't affect high levelled players much. They are a very easy way to obtain unicorn horns in decent quantities, as they are present in greater numbers than normal unicorns. They also have a faster spawn rate and tend to walk around quite a bit in their area, and will sometimes run away when their health is low.

id: category:monsters that retreat when low hitpoints
label: Monsters that retreat when low hitpoints
Black warhammer
title: Black warhammer
lead:
The black warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the steel warhammer. Members can purchase it from Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim and Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka. The black warhammer requires 10 Strength to wield.

The black warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: blackhole
title: blackhole
lead:
The Blackhole, also known as Thordur's blackhole, was Jagex's early punishment system in RuneScape Classic, before the ban system was implemented. Players who misbehaved were sent to the blackhole and would remain there for an undefined amount of time before being removed. It existed throughout most of 2001 until it was removed in December of that same year.

In Old School RuneScape, players are able to visit the blackhole by selecting the "Activate" option on the Disk of returning while in the Dwarven Mines beneath Falador. Here they can interact with Thordur but will be unable to move around. The area and Thordur are not instanced contrary to popular belief, but as there is only 1 available tile in this area, anyone else appearing will be under you. Activating the disk again will return the player to the mines.

label: Blacksmith's tools
title: Blacksmith's tools
lead: Blacksmith's tools are a common piece of decorative scenery, usually found near anvils or in armour shops.

label: Blade (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Blade (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead:
The blade is an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. It consists of a blade coming out of the floor and back down in a cycle. It is the only obstacle in the Agility Arena that requires players to time movement correctly, regardless of Agility level. Crossing the blade will not award any Agility experience.

Players can take damage when standing or walking on the same tile as the incoming blade, even at 99 Agility. The message You were hit by the saw blade! will be displayed if this occurs. The amount of damage is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below.

label: Blamish oil
title: Blamish oil
lead:
Blamish oil is a quest item used in Heroes' Quest. It is made through the Herblore skill, and it turns a normal fishing rod into an oily fishing rod. Oily fishing rods can only be used at lava fishing spots to catch lava eels or infernal eels.

To make blamish oil, combine blamish snail slime with a harralander potion (unf). It requires level 25 Herblore to be made and gives 80 Herblore experience. Completion of Heroes' Quest is not required to create the blamish oil in this way.

label: Blamish snail slime
title: Blamish snail slime
lead:
Blamish snail slime is a quest item in Heroes' Quest. When added to a vial of water with Harralander it makes blamish oil, which can be used on a fishing rod to make an oily fishing rod. The oily fishing rod can then be used to catch lava eels in the Taverley Dungeon or the Lava Maze, or infernal eels in Mor Ul Rek.

Blamish snail slime can be made by going to Mort Myre Swamp, killing a Myre blamish snail, and grinding the raw snail (thin, lean, and fat all work equally) with a pestle and mortar with an empty sample bottle in the player's inventory. Sample bottles can be obtained from the general store in Canifis or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant.

label: Blessed giant rat
title: Blessed giant rat
lead:
The blessed giant rat is a type of giant rat on the second floor in the Underground Pass.

Due to its 30 Hitpoints and low Defence, the blessed giant rat can be good for training Combat on at low levels. It has no drops other than bones, however, and is not in a prime location compared to other giant rats' locations.

label: blessed gold bowl
title: blessed gold bowl
lead:
The blessed gold bowl is a quest item made during or after the Legends' Quest. It is described by Gujuo as a bowl made of the metal of the sun.

The player must make the gold bowl by using two gold bars and a hammer at an anvil while holding the sketch given to the player by Gujuo to make a gold bowl. The bowl can then be taken back to Gujuo to be blessed (must have 42 prayer points, however they will not be consumed), to make it ready for it to hold the holy water needed to free Ungadulu. It is possible to fail when blessing the bowl causing the player to lose 5 prayer points in the process. If the blessed bowl is filled with the sacred pure water of the Kharazi water pool, it becomes a golden bowl containing sacred pure water that can be used with an enchanted vial to make a vial of holy water: one bowl can fill up to 10 vials. After making one successful golden bowl, the player can smith a gold bowl at any anvil, without need of the sketch, for 30 Smithing experience (though there remains a chance of failure); the bowl can then be taken to Gujuo to have it blessed.

label: Blessed spider
title: Blessed spider
lead:
A blessed spider is a type of spider found only in the Underground Pass. They are found on the west side of the bridge and in the pit where Kalrag is located. They are believed to be blessed or "converted" to Iban. Like most spiders, blessed spiders attack with melee and are weak to crush.

Blessed spiders are initially not aggressive to players with a combat level of 78 or above. However, if Kalrag is killed, they become aggressive to players of all levels, and are able to attack the player simultaneously as if they were in a multicombat area. When Kalrag respawns, they revert to being non-aggressive, except for any that might be attempting to attack the player already.

id: category:monsters that take priority in combat
label: Monsters that take priority in combat
Blessed water
title: Blessed water
lead:
Blessed water is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is made by speaking to Drezel to bless the murky water.

It is poured onto the coffin enclosing the vampyre within to allow Drezel to escape from his prison without waking it.

label: Bloated toad
title: Bloated toad
lead:
Bloated toads are used to catch chompy birds during and after the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. Their dyed variant, coloured toads, are used during Mourning's End Part I. Bloated toads can be obtained by using ogre bellows which have been filled with swamp gas on a swamp toad. Only three toads may be obtained at one time, and they cannot be banked.

Bloated toads may only be dropped in the ogre areas east and south of Gu'Tanoth. Once dropped, they have a chance of causing a chompy bird to land, lasting 1 minute before exploding and dealing 1-2 damage to all players within one tile (including diagonally). This damage cannot kill players.

label: Blood rune
title: Blood rune
lead: Blood runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are used in some of the highest level spells, the lowest of which is Ruby Crossbow Bolt Enchant, and the highest is Heal Group. Blood runes are also used in charging the Scythe of Vitur, Sanguinesti staff, Ring of shadows, and soul bearer.

label: blue beret
title: blue beret
lead:
The blue beret is a hat that can be obtained from Easy Treasure Trails. They provide no stat bonuses and are worn purely for cosmetic purposes. There's other variants: the white beret, black beret and red beret.

The examine text, when translated, reads "Do you speak French?"

label: Blue boots
title: Blue boots
lead: Blue boots can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree.

label: Blue cape
title: Blue cape
lead:
A Blue cape can be made by using blue dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.

A blue cape may also be among the items you can obtain from chasing Solus Dellagar during the Wanted! quest, the player calls this cape the "Cape of Champions" during the quest because it is sold in the Champions' Guild.

label: Blue cog
title: Blue cog
lead:
The blue cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found in a rat cage at the end of the path behind a push-able wall, which is accessed through a ladder north-east of the Clock Tower and south of the camel habitat of the Ardougne Zoo.

It is used to repair the southern blue clock spindle on the .

label: Blue d'hide body
title: Blue d'hide body
lead:
A blue d'hide body is a piece of blue dragonhide armour worn in the body slot. It is crafted by using 3 blue dragon leather and a needle and thread with level 71 Crafting. To wear a blue d'hide body, a player must have a Ranged level of 50 and a Defence level of 40.

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear the green d'hide body, completion of this quest is not required to equip the blue, red, and black dragonhide bodies.

label: Blue d'hide chaps
title: Blue d'hide chaps
lead:
Blue d'hide chaps are a piece of the blue dragonhide armour set, and require level 50 Ranged to wear. Similarly to other dragonhide chaps, they have no Defence level requirement.

A player with 68 Crafting can make them using 2 blue dragon leather and 1 thread with a needle, granting 140 experience.

label: Blue d'hide vambraces
title: Blue d'hide vambraces
lead:
Blue d'hide vambraces are a piece of blue d'hide armour worn in the hand slot, which require 50 Ranged to wear. They can be made with a Crafting level of 66.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make blue spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.

label: blue door
title: blue door
lead: The Blue door is located in the basement of Melzar's Maze. It must be opened during Dragon Slayer I, using a blue key obtained from killing one of the nearby Zombies.

label: Blue Dragon
title: Blue Dragon
lead:
Blue dragons are the third strongest of the chromatic dragons, behind red dragons and black dragons. Like all dragons, they can breathe dragonfire, which can inflict up to 50 damage if proper protections aren't used. Dragonfire can be mitigated by equipping an anti-dragon shield or a dragonfire shield – alongside the usage of an antifire potion, which will completely negate dragonfire damage. On top of the strong dragonfire breath, they also attack with an accurate slash attack.

Blue dragons are assignable as a Slayer task after starting Dragon Slayer I. Baby blue dragons also count toward blue dragon tasks, and can be found within the Myths' Guild, Isle of Souls, or the Taverley Dungeon. A variant of blue dragons are found in the Ruins of Tapoyauik that are uniquely weak to fire spells, instead of water like most chromatic dragons.

label: Blue dragon leather
title: Blue dragon leather
lead: Blue dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make blue dragonhide armour. Players can obtain it by taking a blue dragonhide (a drop from blue dragons) and 20 coins to a tanner, or 45 coins for the Canifis tanner. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Crafting Guild, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, and the Forthos Dungeon. Crafting any piece of blue dragonhide armour will grant the player 70 experience per hide.

label: blue dragon scale
title: blue dragon scale
lead: Blue dragon scales are an indirect secondary ingredient in Herblore that is ground with a pestle and mortar to create dragon scale dust, which can then be used to make antifire potions and weapon poison. Scales can be found on the ground by the blue dragons in Taverley Dungeon, Corsair Cove Dungeon, part of the Myths' Guild, in the Isle of Souls Dungeon, and in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. They can also be obtained as an uncommon drop from brutal blue dragons located within the Catacombs of Kourend. All variants of blue dragons also have a chance to drop scaly blue dragonhide, which can be cut with a knife to get 50 blue dragon scales.

label: Blue dragonhide
title: Blue dragonhide
lead:
Blue dragonhide (also known as blue d'hide) is a 100% drop item from blue dragons when killed. Players can take hides to a tanner to make blue dragon leather for a fee of 20 coins at a tanner (45 coins from Sbott in Canifis) or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, the Kebos Lowlands, Auburnvale and the Crafting Guild.

Members can craft pieces of blue dragonhide armour from blue dragon leather with level 66 Crafting.

label: blue dye
title: blue dye
lead:
Blue dye can be obtained from Aggie in Draynor Village in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 5 coins, or from Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 25 coins. It can also be purchased from Oronwen in Lletya, Guinevere in Prifddinas, or Xochitl in Tal Teklan.

Blue dye is mainly used in the Goblin Diplomacy, Land of the Goblins, Ghosts Ahoy and Mourning's End Part I quests. Blue dye can be used with a black cape (or any other colour) to create a blue cape. It can also be used to turn a black robe into a blue robe.

label: Blue flowers
title: Blue flowers
lead:
Blue flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: blue goblin mail
title: blue goblin mail
lead:
Blue goblin mail is made by using blue dye on a goblin mail. Like all goblins mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

It is used during the Goblin Diplomacy quest, along with an orange and un-dyed goblin mail with Generals Bentnoze and Wartface fighting over what colour they prefer.

label: Blue halloween mask
title: Blue halloween mask
lead:
The Blue halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Blue halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After player decided polls, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, this to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3.

label: Blue hat
title: Blue hat
lead: A blue hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree. These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats, as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.

label: Blue hat (Legends' Quest)
title: Blue hat (Legends' Quest)
lead: The blue hat is found in the Viyeldi caves during the Legends' Quest. Trying to pick it up will turn it into Viyeldi, who will recite a poem about what is to come during the quest. After he completes his poem, he disappears and the hat returns in his place.

label: Blue Moon Inn
title: Blue Moon Inn
lead:
The Blue Moon Inn is the tavern and inn in south-central Varrock, marked by a sign at the front and back of the building. The NPCs inside play a role in several quests. Jonny the Beard is involved in the Shield of Arrav quest, Dr Harlow features in the Vampyre Slayer quest, and there is also a treasure chest upstairs that plays a part in Pirate's Treasure. The establishment is repeatedly described as the "Blue moon pub" by Charlie the Tramp in the Shield of Arrav quest. It is called the "Blue Moon inn" by Aris.

The Blue Moon Inn is featured in the Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl miniquest.

label: Blue partyhat
title: Blue partyhat
lead:
Blue partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

It can be sewn with sagacious spectacles to make Partyhat & specs by talking to Patchy, along with 500 coins. Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' piracy.

label: Blue robe bottoms
title: Blue robe bottoms
lead: Blue robe bottoms can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions. You can find Rometti on the of the Grand Tree, in the north-eastern area.

label: Blue robe top
title: Blue robe top
lead: A blue robe top can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree.

label: Blue Sheep
title: Blue Sheep
lead:
Blue Sheep are sick sheep found near the Moss giants, south-east of Baxtorian Falls that must be prodded with the cattleprod to the sheep pen and fed the poisoned sheep feed during the Sheep Herder quest. Its wool is slightly bluish. Once killed, it drops the sheep bones (3).

After Mourning's End Part I, the sheep are of a darker blue as a result of the player dyeing them with a Fixed device loaded with a Blue toad. Once dyed, they can no longer be prodded or interacted with in any way. Luckily, players only need to dye one and all the sheep of the same colour turn dark. This is how players can tell they haven't missed the sheep during the quest.

label: Blue skirt
title: Blue skirt
lead:
A blue skirt is clothing that provides no bonuses. It can be purchased at Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock for coins.

Although the skirt aesthetically matches the Blue wizard hat and Blue wizard robe, the blue skirt offers no bonuses. Zamorak monk bottoms, however, are the only leg slot item with offensive magic bonuses in free-to-play.

label: Blue wizard hat
title: Blue wizard hat
lead: A blue wizard hat is low-level armour that provides a small Magic attack and Defence bonus. This hat can also be dyed into a black wizard hat by using black dye.

label: Blue wizard robe
title: Blue wizard robe
lead:
A blue wizard robe is the most basic piece of chest armour for low level Magic users. It can be turned into a black robe by using black dye on it; similarly, it can be created by using blue dye on a black robe.

The blue robe is often worn with the blue wizard hat and blue skirt for aesthetics.

label: Blurberry
title: Blurberry
lead: Blurberry is the barman running the Blurberry Bar. Players must speak to him before being allowed to play the Gnome Restaurant minigame. He is also used to get the drink required to complete the Recipe for Disaster quest. He is found on the of the Grand Tree, just east of the ladder in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. You can speak to him using the NPC Contact spell.

label: Blurberry Bar
title: Blurberry Bar
lead:
Blurberry Bar is located inside the Grand Tree in the Gnome Stronghold. To get there, the player must climb to the and turn east. Players may talk to Blurberry to learn the art of gnome cuisine, which will then allow players to begin playing the minigame Gnome Restaurant. The barman sells premade drinks as well as lemons, oranges, and cocktail shakers via dialogue. These premade drinks cannot be used for the Gnome Restaurant minigame or for the quest Recipe for Disaster. This bar is featured in the Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl.

There is a second Blurberry's bar upstairs, east of the Gnome Ball field with identical stock and prices.

label: Blurberry bar (scenery)
title: Blurberry bar (scenery)
lead: Blurberry bars are the counters belonging to the two Blurberry Bars in the Tree Gnome Stronghold, found just east of the Gnome Ball field and in the Grand Tree.

label: Blurberry special
title: Blurberry special
lead:
The Blurberry special can be mixed with 1 vodka, 1 brandy, 1 gin, 1 orange, and 2 lemons. It can be finished by adding 1 equa leaf, 1 sliced lime, 1 diced lemon, and 1 diced orange as a garnish. This requires 37 Cooking to make.

All of these ingredients can be purchased at Funch's Fine Groceries and cost a total of 30 coins per Blurberry special made (not including cocktail shaker, cocktail glass, or knife). A Premade blurb' sp. (premade Blurberry special) can be purchased at the Blurberry Bar for 30 coins.

label: Blurite ore
title: Blurite ore
lead:
Blurite ore is a quest item used in The Knight's Sword. It can be mined at level 10 Mining, and grants 17.5 Mining experience when mined. After being mined, a blurite ore rock takes approximately 25 seconds to respawn.

Rocks containing blurite are found only in the mine in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, located south of Port Sarim on the tip of the Asgarnian Peninsula and north of Mudskipper Point (Fairy ring ). The Ice Caves are guarded by Ice warriors and Ice giants, both of which can hit up to 7. Although blurite ore is mineable by non-members, only members can smith it. Thus, it is worthless to non-members except for doing The Knight's Sword.

label: blurite rocks
title: blurite rocks
lead:
Blurite rock is a rock that, when mined, gives blurite ore, which can be used in the making of the hilt of the blurite sword in The Knight's Sword quest and in crossbows and bolts. It can be mined by a player with level 10 Mining.
Blurite rocks can only be found in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon mine in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, located south of Port Sarim on the tip of the Asgarnian Peninsula.

Low-level players should take caution before entering the caves due to the presence of Ice warriors and Ice giants. However, there is a safespot. Situated right in front of the blurite ore is a single stalagmite. You can mine one of the rocks from directly behind it and trap all attackers on the other side. To get the other rock, you may run around, mine it, and situate yourself back in the safespot.

label: Blurite sword
title: Blurite sword
lead:
The blurite sword is a longsword quest item used only in The Knight's Sword. It requires 1 Attack to wield, and is obtained by giving a blurite ore and two iron bars to Thurgo after showing him a portrait of the sword.

The blurite sword has the same attack and defence bonuses as a steel longsword with the strength bonus of an iron longsword. It is slightly worse than Silverlight. Because of this and the fact that there is no Attack level needed to wield it, the blurite sword is sought by some lower level players at the start of the game.

label: Boarded-up door
title: Boarded-up door
lead: A boarded-up door is located south of Ardougne in the Clock Tower, which is the location of the quest Clock Tower. The scenery object is actually the boards in front of the door, which are present on both sides.

label: Bob
title: Bob
lead:
Bob is the owner of Bob's Brilliant Axes in southern Lumbridge. Players can pay Bob to repair damaged Barrows equipment and Moon equipment. However, many players prefer to repair their Barrows armour at an armour stand in a player-owned house because it is usually cheaper depending on the player's Smithing level.

Bob also plays a small role in The Lost Tribe, where he may be one of several townsfolk who mentions seeing a goblin with bulging eyes go through a hole in the Lumbridge Castle basement. He also plays a role in Death to the Dorgeshuun, where he expresses strong disgust towards the Dorgeshuun, screaming at the player and Zanik "Get out of my shop! GET OUT!" [...] We don't serve the likes of that thing in here.

label: Bob (cat)
title: Bob (cat)
lead:
Bob the Jagex cat is an enigmatic black cat who travels the world of Gielinor with his girlfriend, Neite, although he generally returns to his human Unferth's house every week. Like all cats, his speech can only be understood through the use of the catspeak amulet.

As Bob likes to wander the world, he has one of the largest wander radius of all NPCs in the game, spawning outside his human Unferth's house in Burthorpe every time there is a system update, after which he is allowed to roam up to 30,000 tiles in any direction. As Bob is essentially able to wander anywhere that is not restricted by physical boundaries, players can run into him at places as far away as Edgeville, Port Sarim, the Wise Old Man's house, or even Lumbridge's church. It is possible to locate Bob by using the catspeak amulet after it is enchanted in A Tail of Two Cats which, when operated, will open a menu that looks like a cat's face. By clicking on the whiskers, the dial will rotate. When the eyes light up and a cat meowing sound is heard, Bob can be found in the direction that the dial is pointing.

label: Bob (Sinclair)
title: Bob (Sinclair)
lead:
Bob Sinclair is one of Lord Sinclair's children. He is a suspect in the Murder Mystery quest.

According to the Gossip, he suffers from severe tea addiction, drinking up to 20 cups of tea per day. In order to supplement his addiction, he has spent all his allowance and stole some silverware from the kitchen in order to pawn them to purchase his tea. He can be found in the garden on the Sinclair family residence.

label: Bob's barrel
title: Bob's barrel
lead: Bob's barrel can be found inside the Sinclair Mansion in Bob's bedroom. During the Murder Mystery quest, the player must search the barrel to find his Silver cup.

label: Bob's Brilliant Axes.
title: Bob's Brilliant Axes.
lead: Bob's Brilliant Axes is located in southern Lumbridge. It is the only shop in the city apart from the general store. Bob is also one of five NPCs that can repair Barrows equipment.

label: Bob's print
title: Bob's print
lead: Bob's print is a quest item in the Murder Mystery quest. It is created by using flypaper on the silver cup after dusting it with a pot of flour. If the prints match those of the unknown print, it will become a killer's print, meaning Bob is the killer.

label: Body Altar
title: Body Altar
lead:
The Body Altar is a runic altar upon which body runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 7.5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Players can also use a body core to craft body runes, which provides 75 Runecraft experience per core. Level 20 Runecraft is required to craft body runes.

Players may create a body tiara here by using either a body talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 37.5 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 60 Runecraft experience.

label: Body rune
title: Body rune
lead:
Body runes are low level runes used for confuse, weaken, curse and Monster Inspect spells in the standard spellbook, as well as Dream and Stat Spy in the Lunar spellbook. They are also used for the reanimation spells Basic Reanimation and Adept Reanimation in the Arceuus spellbook.

Body runes can be created using Runecraft skill at level 20 at the Body Altar south of Edgeville Monastery, providing 7.5 Runecraft experience per essence. They are the highest level rune Free to Play players can craft.

label: Body talisman
title: Body talisman
lead:
A body talisman is a talisman used in the Runecraft skill. It allows players to enter the Body Altar and create body runes from rune, pure, or daeyalt essence.

At the Body Altar, a body talisman can be combined with a tiara to make a body tiara for 37.5 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the body tiara also grants access to the Body Altar when worn.

label: Bolkoy
title: Bolkoy
lead: Bolkoy is a gnome who is found by climbing up a ladder in the Tree Gnome Village, he runs Bolkoy's Village Shop, the village's general store.

label: Bolkoy's Village Shop
title: Bolkoy's Village Shop
lead:
Bolkoy's Village Shop is a general store on the of the Tree Gnome Village, owned by Bolkoy. It can be accessed before completing the Tree Gnome Village quest.

A poll booth can be found next to the shop.

label: Bone beads
title: Bone beads
lead: Bone beads are a quest item that are obtained during the Shilo Village quest by using a chisel on the sword pommel found in the tomb of Beverius. When combined with bronze wire they form a beads of the dead necklace that can be used to protect the player in Rashiliyia's Tomb. There are only three beads in the inventory icon, yet there are five on the necklace.

label: Bone key (Shilo Village)
title: Bone key (Shilo Village)
lead:
Bone key is used in the Shilo Village quest to open and enter Rashiliyia's Tomb. It can be made by using a chisel on a bone shard. Besides this function, it has no further use besides selling it to Yanni Salika for 100 coins.

The bone key can be added to the steel key ring to save bank space. Attempting to drop it will result in the chatbox stating This looks quite valuable. As you go to throw the item away Zadimus' words come to you again. 'I am the key, but only kin may approach her'.

label: Bone shard (Shilo Village)
title: Bone shard (Shilo Village)
lead:
The bone shard is a quest item that is given to the player by the spirit of Zadimus during the Shilo Village quest. When the player buries the corpse of Zadimus next to the tribal totem in Tai Bwo Wannai, Zadimus's spirit appears and thanks the player. The bone shard then emerges from the soil.

If the shard is dropped, it will crumble to dust, and players will have to retrieve Zadimus' corpse from the temple (rumoured to be Ah Za Rhoon) and bury it again.

label: Bone Yard
title: Bone Yard
lead:
The Bone Yard is located in level 32 Wilderness, and is populated by aggressive level 25 skeletons. It is notable for the large amounts of bones and big bones that can be found there. Due to the fast respawn rate of the bones there, the Bone Yard is an effective way for free-to-play players to train Prayer, by picking up and burying the bones and big bones as they spawn.

Players intending to train Prayer at the Bone Yard are recommended to only bring items they are willing to lose, due to its dangerous location and inhabitants. Armour and food can help to mitigate the damage taken from the skeletons until they lose their aggressiveness after 10 minutes, however it may be beneficial to discard them after this due to their added weight increasing the player's run energy drain rate. In total, there are six big bones spawns and 34 bones spawns at the Bone Yard.

label: Bones
title: Bones
lead:
Bones are the remains of most creatures with an animalistic or humanoid appearance.

Bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 13.5 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 13.5 XP when using the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 15.7 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 31.4 per bone.
* 18 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of bonemeal.
* 20 XP when blessed, broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed wine, or 24 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

label: Bones (Tutorial Island)
title: Bones (Tutorial Island)
lead:
Bones are a unique variant of bones that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island. They can be obtained by killing Giant rats, but this is not required to progress in the tutorial.

A second variant of the bones could be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

label: Bones to Bananas
title: Bones to Bananas
lead:
Bones to Bananas is a spell that can be used to turn all normal bones, burnt bones, bat bones, bleached bones, jogre bones, wolf bones, monkey bones, Alan's bones, animals' bones, and big bones in the inventory into bananas. It requires two water runes, two earth runes, and one Nature rune to be cast, with a Magic level of 15. This spell can be useful when fighting monsters which drop bones as a 100% drop, as the bananas produced heal 2 Hitpoints each.

If you are casting the spell only for magic experience, add only one bone to your inventory at a time as it turns ALL bones in inventory into bananas for only 25 exp per spell regardless of number of bones. At least one bone or big bone must be in your inventory to be able to cast the spell.

label: Bonzo
title: Bonzo
lead: Bonzo is the fishing contest judge located in the fishing area west of Seers' Village. He is used during the Fishing Contest quest, where he collects the players' entry fee and judges the fish they catch.

label: Book (Plague City)
title: Book (Plague City)
lead:
Turnip Growing for Beginners known as Book in-game is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is obtained from Jethick after showing him a picture of Elena.

It is given to Ted Rehnison in northern West Ardougne in order to enter their home.

label: Book (Shield of Arrav)
title: Book (Shield of Arrav)
lead: A book, titled The Shield of Arrav, is an item obtained during the Shield of Arrav quest. It can be found by searching the bookcase on the eastern side of the centre shelves of Varrock Palace Library. The book was written by A R Wright who details the history of the Shield of Arrav and how it fell into the hands of the Phoenix Gang. It can be stored in the bookcase of a Player-owned house.

label: Book of Spells
title: Book of Spells
lead:
Book of Spells is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Autumn Voyage, Dream, Flute Salad, Harmony, and Yesteryear.

In Classic mode, the track plays in the western part of Lumbridge Swamp.

label: Book on baxtorian
title: Book on baxtorian
lead:
The Book on baxtorian can be found by searching a bookcase in the Tourist Information Centre just south of the Baxtorian Falls. In it is a brief history on Baxtorian, his treasure, and the reason he hid himself away beneath the waterfall, as well as a lot of useful hints and information concerning how a player might get in to retrieve the treasure.

The book is used in the Waterfall Quest and after finding the book it can be found on the shelves in a player-owned house. It can also be found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

label: Book on chemicals
title: Book on chemicals
lead:
The Book on chemicals, or Volatile chemicals - Experimental Test Notes, is part of The Dig Site quest. It has some information on how to make a Chemical compound that can be used to destroy some blocks.

After the quest it can be found on the shelves in your house.

label: Bookcase (Draynor Manor)
title: Bookcase (Draynor Manor)
lead: The bookcase in Draynor Manor can be searched to open a secret door leading to the room in which Ava is located. The room behind the bookcase plays a central role in the quest Animal Magnetism. The room is also used to access the basement in the quest Ernest the Chicken. To leave the room again, the nearby lever must be pulled to open the secret door.

label: Bookcase (Elemental Workshop I)
title: Bookcase (Elemental Workshop I)
lead: The bookcase can be found on the eastern wall of the building located south-west of the Seers' Village bank. Searching the bookcase results in the player finding a battered book, which when read starts the Elemental Workshop I quest and can be cut open to obtain a battered key. Subsequent searches of the bookcase after cutting open the book will result in the player finding a slashed book and the battered key if either have been lost.

label: Bookcase (Shaman Caves)
title: Bookcase (Shaman Caves)
lead:
The Bookcase is found in the Shaman Caves and encountered during Legends' Quest. It can be searched in order to find a small crevice in the wall, allowing players with an Agility level of at least 50 to proceed further through the caves. Failing to squeeze through the crevice will result in the player's Agility level temporarily being lowered.

Searching the bookcase results in the message: "After perusing the empty bookcase for a while, you decide to check behind it. There's a crevice in the wall! You might just be able to force your way though if you were in any way athletic."

label: Bookcase (Shield of Arrav)
title: Bookcase (Shield of Arrav)
lead: The bookcase is located on the east side of the centre bookcases in the library of Varrock Palace. The bookcase is used during the quest Shield of Arrav to obtain a book detailing the history of the Shield of Arrav. It is distinguishable from the other shelves in the library, due having a blue book with a white cross on the top shelf.

label: bookcase (The Tourist Trap)
title: bookcase (The Tourist Trap)
lead: Bookcase is a scenery object found in south-western corner on the of Captain Siad's office in the Desert Mining Camp. During The Tourist Trap quest, players must search the bookcase to discover Siad's love of sailing. After which, players can distract the captain by having him talk about sailing, allowing them to open his chest to obtain the technical plans.

label: Bookcase (Waterfall Quest)
title: Bookcase (Waterfall Quest)
lead: The bookcase is the southernmost bookcase on the eastern wall of the Tourist Information Centre's . The bookcase is used during the Waterfall Quest, in which the player must search it to obtain a book detailing the brief history of Baxtorian and his treasure. Should a player lose their copy of the book, they can search the bookcase again to find another one.

label: Bookshelves
title: Bookshelves
lead: Bookshelves is a piece of scenery found in the Underground Pass in Kardia's house. It serves no purpose other than decoration.

label: Boot
title: Boot
lead:
Boot the Dwarf is a dwarf found in the Dwarven Mines. He plays a small part in the Family Crest quest.

The only thing he will do for players is tell them about the origin of his name. When he was young, he was so small that he slept in a boot. However, the player cuts him off before he can finish his story.

label: Boots of lightness
title: Boots of lightness
lead: Boots of lightness reduce weight by 4.535 kg when worn, and offer slight defensive bonuses. As they are easy to obtain in bulk, they may be safely used in the wilderness. While they grant a higher weight-reduction than the graceful boots, they do not give an increase to run energy restoration rate.

label: Border Guard
title: Border Guard
lead:
Border Guards patrol the border gate between eastern Lumbridge and north-western Al Kharid, charging an entry fee of 10gp provided the player has not completed Prince Ali Rescue. Once the quest has been completed, the right click option "pay-toll-10gp" is still effective, and will not charge the fee.

They appear to be wielding a steel halberd.

label: Boulder (Shaman Caves)
title: Boulder (Shaman Caves)
lead: Three boulders can be found in the Shaman Caves between the first and second ancient gates. The boulders can be smashed to bits with a Mining level of 52, giving the player a rock each time one of them is smashed. Smashing a boulder results in the player automatically walking past where it stood, a new rock then drops down behind them. Failing to smash a boulder will result in the player's mining level temporarily being lowered by one.

label: Boulder (Viyeldi caves)
title: Boulder (Viyeldi caves)
lead: Three boulders can be found in the Viyeldi caves during the Legends' Quest. One boulder must be pushed during the quest to access the sacred water. The first time one of the boulders is pushed, a spirit called Echned Zekin will appear and give the player a dark dagger and ask them to kill Viyeldi with it. The second time a boulder is pushed, Nezikchened will spawn and attack the player.

label: Bouncer
title: Bouncer
lead:
Bouncer is a hellhound that is fought during the Fight Arena quest. He is the pet of General Khazard. It is possible to range or mage him from behind the skeletons that lie scattered around the arena. It is also possible to use a halberd to attack him from one of these safespots. Being a hellhound, he is vulnerable to demonbane weapons and counts as a hellhound for Slayer tasks.

Note: 10 HP accounts require Guthix rests in order to kill Bouncer. Bouncer's Max Hit is 13, which is also the HP given by a Saradomin brew. Through both the use of Ring of recoil and Dynamite(p), Bouncer IS killable.

label: Bow (emote)
title: Bow (emote)
lead:
Bow is the third listed emote. Upon use the player bows with their right hand crossing over the waist.

When using the "Loop" option the player performs and holds the bow.

label: Bow and Arrow salesman
title: Bow and Arrow salesman
lead: The Bow and Arrow salesman, real name Dargaud, is a vendor who is located in the Ranging Guild west of Seers' Village. He runs Dargaud's Bow and Arrows. ranging equipment shop.

label: Bow string
title: Bow string
lead:
A bow string is used in the Fletching skill to create bows. It is created by using flax on a spinning wheel, or by casting the Spin Flax spell.

Using a spinning wheel, it takes approximately 50 seconds to spin a full inventory of 28 flax, requiring 10 Crafting and granting a total of 420 experience.

label: Bowl
title: Bowl
lead:
A bowl is a vessel used primarily in Cooking to hold water, stew, curry, kebab mix, etc.

Bowls can be created by using a piece of soft clay on a potter's wheel and then firing the unfired bowl in a pottery oven. Players may also choose to take bowls from the Mess Hall utensil cupboard and bank them at the bank chest to the south-east.

label: Bowl of water
title: Bowl of water
lead:
A bowl of water is made by using a normal bowl on a water source that is not a well. The Humidify spell will also turn any empty bowls the player is carrying into bowls of water. Players can use a bowl of water on a stove or a fire to create a bowl of hot water.

Adding some nettles will make it into nettle-water, and if this is heated it will turn into nettle tea. You also can make an incomplete stew by using a potato on the bowl of water, and people do this to make easy profit. Bowls of water, just like buckets and jugs of water, can be combined with pots of flour to make any kind of dough, though this is less commonly done.

label: Boxes (Elemental Workshop)
title: Boxes (Elemental Workshop)
lead: Boxes are scenery found in the north-eastern part of the entrance room in the Elemental Workshop. They can be searched for a stone bowl during the Elemental Workshop I quest.

label: boy
title: boy
lead:
The boy in Taverley is the starting point for the Witch's House quest. He can be found just south of Nora T. Hagg's house.

He accidentally kicked his ball into Nora's garden, and rather than giving it back to him, she became angry at the boy for being so careless and locked it in her shed. At the boy's request, players infiltrate Nora's house and return his ball.

label: Brandy
title: Brandy
lead: Brandy is an alcoholic drink which can be purchased at Jossik's store in the Lighthouse, at the Tree Gnome Stronghold in Heckel Funch's store or at the Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach. It is an ingredient in the gnome cocktail Blurberry special. It heals 5 hitpoints, increases a player's Strength by 5% + 1 and decreases Attack by 2% - 3 when drunk. Unlike the other types of alcoholic drinks bought from stores, brandy has a cone-shaped bottle.

label: Brass key
title: Brass key
lead:
The brass key is a key which allows the player to enter the locked shed found west of the Cooking Guild. The shed provides an alternate entrance to the Edgeville Dungeon, entering north of the Hill Giant room.

To get the key, you must enter the Edgeville Dungeon through the entrance south of the Edgeville bank and make your way through the dungeon. Just north of the hill giant room, there is a small circular room with the key on the ground. It re-spawns every minute.

label: Brass necklace
title: Brass necklace
lead: A brass necklace is a near-worthless item worn purely for aesthetic purposes, as it offers no combat bonuses. It cannot be made using the Crafting skill, and is dropped by goblins. It spawns in two locations: Edgeville Dungeon near the hobgoblins, and the downstairs area of Varrock west bank (requires Telekinetic grab or completion of Crack the Clue III to obtain).

label: Bravek
title: Bravek
lead: Bravek is the city warder of West Ardougne. He can be found on the ground floor of the Civic Office of West Ardougne.

label: bravery potion
title: bravery potion
lead:
The bravery potion is made during Legends' Quest, and is used to overcome the magical fear that blocks access to the dark cave in the Kharazi Dungeon. A player only needs to drink this potion once to gain unlimited access to the dark cave.

To make this potion, players will need a vial of water, one ardrigal, and one snake weed. Although 45 Herblore is listed as a requirement for Legends' Quest, it is not required to make the bravery potion.

label: Bread
title: Bread
lead: Bread is a type of food that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking bread dough on a cooking range, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt bread. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Bread is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range. Bread may also be bought or stolen from the Ardougne Baker's Stall in the Ardougne marketplace.

label: Bread dough
title: Bread dough
lead: Bread dough is made by mixing either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water with a pot of flour. It can be used on a range to make a loaf of bread at level 1 Cooking, granting 40 experience and healing 5 hitpoints when consumed. It is one of the most basic items used for the Cooking skill. Players will also get a pot of flour and a bucket of water to make bread dough on Tutorial Island, as a tutorial for cooking.

label: Breoca
title: Breoca
lead: Breoca is a citizen of Burthorpe.

label: Brew Barrel
title: Brew Barrel
lead: The Brew Barrels are found in one of the houses at the bottom of the Underground Pass, and on the eastern wall of Castle Wars. During the Underground Pass quest, the player must fill a bucket with dwarf brew from the barrel, as the brew is required to light a pyre on the tomb of Iban. The barrel on the eastern wall of Castle Wars cannot be reached, as there are multiple crates blocking the way.

label: Brian
title: Brian
lead:
Brian is a shop owner who runs Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim. He sells battleaxes, from bronze to adamant.

He also plays a small role in the One Small Favour quest, agreeing to sharpen the jungle forester's axe if Aggie can become a witness for his friend, who was jailed during a pub fight.

label: Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar.
title: Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar.
lead: Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar is located in Port Sarim and owned by Brian. It is one of the two battleaxe stores in RuneScape - the other is located in Lumbridge. The shop stocks battleaxes from bronze to adamant.

label: Bridge (Iban's Lair)
title: Bridge (Iban's Lair)
lead:
A series of bridges interrupt the narrow footpaths within the suspended maze leading up to Iban's Temple, at the very heart of the Underground Pass dungeon.

There is no Agility level requirement to cross the bridges, and a successful crossing does not grant any experience. If the player fails to make the jump, they will fall into the large subcavern below and land amidst the soulless, taking up to 24 points of damage in the process. They will then have to use the staircase in the north-western corner in order to climb back up.

label: Bridge (Nature Grotto)
title: Bridge (Nature Grotto)
lead: The bridge is a structure found outside the Nature Grotto that the player must jump over to reach Filliman Tarlock and the grotto dungeon. Attempting to jump the bridge requires 1 Agility, granting 15 experience. If the jump is failed, the player will receive 1-7 damage and 2 experience. Failing the jump will still place the player on the other side of the bridge.

label: Brimhaven
title: Brimhaven
lead: Brimhaven is a members-only pirate town located on north-western Karamja, led by the wealthy Scarface Pete. Although it is mainly inhabited by pirates, it's also the home of Sandy's Sand Corporation and contains outposts of two Varrockian crime gangs aiming to rob the pirate leader. The street from The Shrimp and Parrot restaurant to Davon's Amulet Store is called Palm Street.

label: Brimhaven Agility Arena
title: Brimhaven Agility Arena
lead: The Brimhaven Agility Course is an Agility-training minigame located beneath Brimhaven, this course has no requirements except for the entrance fee. On this course, it is possible to get upwards of 67,000 Agility experience per hour at level 99 Agility (due to no longer failing any obstacles at 99 Agility). At lower Agility levels expect to get around 50,000–60,000 Agility experience per hour, depending on Agility and concentration levels.

label: Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange
title: Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange
lead:
The Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange is the former rewards shop for the Brimhaven Agility Arena minigame, accessed by talking to Pirate Jackie the Fruit at the minigame's entrance. At the ticket exchange, players could exchange the discontinued Agility arena tickets earned in the minigame for Agility experience, various items, and a recolour for the graceful outfit.

The store was replaced by the Agility Arena Store, however it remains accessible to players who still have the historical Agility arena tickets to redeem for rewards.

label: Brimstail
title: Brimstail
lead:
Brimstail is a gnome wizard that lives in a small cave in the south-west part of Tree Gnome Stronghold, near the river. He can teleport a player to the Rune essence mine if they have completed Rune Mysteries.

Brimstail is one of the few gnomes that uses magic. He dabbles in the gnomish art of illusionment spells, and is actually in possession of the machine that Oaknock used to prove the death of Argento the spirit tree.

label: Brimstail's cave
title: Brimstail's cave
lead:
Brimstail's cave is a small cave found in the south-western section of the Tree Gnome Stronghold. It is the home of Brimstail, a gnome wizard. It is the starting point of, and plays a large role in, The Eyes of Glouphrie quest. From here, by talking to Brimstail, players can travel to the rune essence mine. However this is not commonly used due to its distance from a bank.

The cave is accessed via the Cave entrance, a unique hillside door not found anywhere else in Gielinor.

label: Broken armour
title: Broken armour
lead:
Broken armour can only be found by digging in the Digsite. It can be repaired at an armour stand in the workshop of a player-owned house. It will give 25 Smithing experience and become a platelegs or plateskirt of random metal, from bronze to mithril. Also, there is a chance of breaking it beyond repair.

When shown to Terry Balando at the Exam Centre in Misthalin, he says "...the wearer of this fought a mighty battle."

label: Broken arrow
title: Broken arrow
lead:
A broken arrow can be found in certain item spawn points, such as in the Ranging Guild and playing the Fishing Trawler minigame. An Ava's accumulator can also randomly attract one to the player's inventory. If it is caught during Fishing Trawler, then the player will receive 5 Fishing experience. Searching certain boxes on the table during the King's Ransom quest provides unlimited broken arrows.

Broken arrows, along with broken staves and broken armour can be repaired at a repair bench in a player-owned house. Successfully repairing a broken arrow gives 8 Fletching experience and creates up to a mithril arrow. Failing to repair the broken arrow destroys it.

label: Broken axe (adamant)
title: Broken axe (adamant)
lead:
A broken adamant axe was an adamant axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge for 107 coins.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (black)
title: Broken axe (black)
lead:
A broken black axe was a black axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge for 10 coins.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (bronze)
title: Broken axe (bronze)
lead:
A broken bronze axe was a bronze axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (iron)
title: Broken axe (iron)
lead:
A broken iron axe was an iron axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (mithril)
title: Broken axe (mithril)
lead:
A broken mithril axe was a mithril axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge for 18 coins.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (rune)
title: Broken axe (rune)
lead:
A broken rune axe was a rune axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge for 427 coins.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken axe (steel)
title: Broken axe (steel)
lead:
A broken steel axe was a steel axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

label: Broken cart
title: Broken cart
lead: Broken carts are scenery objects found throughout Gielinor. Players cannot interact with these carts, but they can examine them. During the Monk's Friend quest, the player must give Brother Cedric logs in order to repair his nearby broken cart.

label: Broken fence (Lumber Yard)
title: Broken fence (Lumber Yard)
lead: A broken fence can be found as part of the southern fence of the Lumber Yard. The broken fence must be climbed-over in order to enter the Lumber Yard.

label: Broken glass
title: Broken glass
lead:
Broken glass is an item which is the result of some glass being broken. Its main use is during the Sea Slug quest, where the player must use the glass on the damp sticks to get dry sticks, which have a "Rub-together" option to light a torch needed to continue with the quest.

It also plays a minor role in the Client of Kourend, In Aid of the Myreque, and Forgettable Tale... quests. In Client of Kourend, broken glass is obtained as a result of activating the mysterious orb near the Dark Altar. During Forgettable Tale..., the rowdy dwarf requests a random item in exchange for his Kelda seed, with broken glass being a possible item he requests. Broken glass is also one of the junk items found during In Aid of the Myreque when mining rubble piles.

label: Broken glass (unobtainable item)
title: Broken glass (unobtainable item)
lead:
Broken glass is an item that could originally be obtained when searching soil in the Digsite. Although it was obtainable in RuneScape Classic and early RuneScape 2, at some point the soil was changed to give the standard broken glass found at the Fishing Platform. It is unknown exactly when this occurred, but it was possibly with the rework of The Dig Site on 22 August 2006.

It may also have been obtainable by searching various chests or sacks, which would provide various pieces of junk. This feature was removed in an update on 27 September 2006.

label: Broken log raft
title: Broken log raft
lead:
A broken log raft is on the Baxtorian Falls above the entrance to the Waterfall Dungeon and another is on the small island north-east of Fossil Island.

A broken log raft can also be seen briefly when exiting the Ah Za Rhoon cave during Shilo Village.

label: Broken pickaxe (adamant)
title: Broken pickaxe (adamant)
lead:
A broken adamant pickaxe was an adamant pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 107 coins.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken pickaxe (bronze)
title: Broken pickaxe (bronze)
lead:
A broken bronze pickaxe was a bronze pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken pickaxe (iron)
title: Broken pickaxe (iron)
lead:
A broken iron pickaxe was an iron pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 50 coins.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken pickaxe (mithril)
title: Broken pickaxe (mithril)
lead:
A broken mithril pickaxe was a mithril pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 43 coins.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken pickaxe (rune)
title: Broken pickaxe (rune)
lead:
A broken rune pickaxe was a rune pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 1,100 coins.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken pickaxe (steel)
title: Broken pickaxe (steel)
lead:
A broken steel pickaxe was a steel pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock. It could be fixed at Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 17 coins.

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

label: Broken shield
title: Broken shield
lead:
The broken shield is one of the two halves of the restored Shield of Arrav.

In the Shield of Arrav quest, the player must combine both parts of the broken shield to get the complete shield. One player must join the Black Arm Gang and retrieve the right half from a cupboard upstairs in the base. The other player must be in the Phoenix Gang and must get the left half from the chest in the underground base.

label: Broken staff
title: Broken staff
lead:
A broken staff is an item that can be repaired into different kinds of staves at a repair bench or higher in the workshop of a player-owned house. Repairing one gives 14.5 Crafting experience.

Broken staves can be dug up at the Digsite or fished up on the Fishing Trawler.

label: Bronze 2h sword
title: Bronze 2h sword
lead:
The bronze 2h sword is the weakest two-handed sword in Old School RuneScape. Like all bronze weaponry, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

It can be created at level 14 Smithing by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory, granting 37.5 Smithing experience.

label: Bronze arrow
title: Bronze arrow
lead:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

label: Bronze arrowtips
title: Bronze arrowtips
lead:
Bronze arrowtips are made with a bronze bar requiring 5 Smithing, yielding 12.5 Smithing experience and 15 bronze arrowtips. They are made into bronze arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 1 Fletching, yielding 19.5 Fletching experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for coin at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Armoury in the Combat Training Camp, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.

label: Bronze axe
title: Bronze axe
lead:
The Bronze axe is the weakest axe in Old School RuneScape. It can be wielded for combat, or used to cut trees in Woodcutting. It requires an Attack level of 1 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 1 to be used.

Players can make a bronze axe with the Smithing skill at level 1 using one Bronze bar, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can take one for free from logs found at various locations, such as at the chicken farm by the Lumbridge cow field, or Fred the Farmer's house. One can also be obtained by talking to the Woodsman tutor.

label: Bronze axe head
title: Bronze axe head
lead:
The bronze axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: bronze bar
title: bronze bar
lead:
A bronze bar is a bar of refined bronze. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 1 by using a copper ore and a tin ore on a furnace, granting 6.2 Smithing experience. A bronze bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create bronze weapons and armour. A list of bronze items that can be smithed from bronze bars and the Smithing levels required can be found here. When smithed, each bar gives 12.5 experience, with a maximum of 62.5 experience given for the bronze platebody.

Members can purchase bronze bars from the Shantay Pass Shop in the Shantay Pass south of Al Kharid for 8gp each, or from Jiminua's Jungle Store north of Tai Bwo Wannai village for 12gp each.

label: bronze battleaxe
title: bronze battleaxe
lead: The bronze battleaxe is a battleaxe made of bronze. The weakest battleaxe in the game, it requires 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze battleaxe with the Smithing skill at level 10 using 3 bronze bars, giving 37.5 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim.

label: Bronze bolts
title: Bronze bolts
lead:
Bronze bolts are the weakest bolts, and may be shot from any crossbow.

Bronze bolts are crossbow bolts made out of bronze. To make them, a player must smith unfinished bronze bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 3, and for each bronze bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished bronze bolts and 12 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 9 and 1 feather, granting 0.5 Fletching experience per bolt. They may also be stolen from the crossbow stall in Keldagrim. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

label: Bronze chainbody
title: Bronze chainbody
lead: The bronze chainbody is a chainbody that can be made at an anvil with 3 bronze bars and a hammer with a Smithing level of 11, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. Since it requires a Defence level of 1 to wear, it can be worn by any player. It is one of the weakest armour chest pieces in the game and is seldom worn. The bronze chainbody can be obtained through a spawn located in the Dwarven Mine.

label: Bronze claws
title: Bronze claws
lead:
Bronze claws are a two-handed melee weapon, and are the weakest set of claws available. They can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Bronze claws can be obtained either by using the Smithing skill to make a pair, or buying them from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den. The requirements for making them are completing the Death Plateau quest and level 13 Smithing. To make them, use two bronze bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 experience.

label: Bronze dagger
title: Bronze dagger
lead: The bronze dagger is the most basic dagger in Old School RuneScape, and can be made at an anvil using the Smithing skill. This requires one bronze bar and a hammer, and yields 12.5 Smithing experience. There are no level requirements to create or wield a bronze dagger; like many melee weapons, it can be poisoned.

label: Bronze dart
title: Bronze dart
lead:
Bronze darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from bronze that are only available to members. Bronze darts only require level 1 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Bronze darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Players can smith bronze bars into bronze dart tips with level 4 Smithing after completion of The Tourist Trap. Each bronze bar creates 10 bronze dart tips and gives the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added with at least level 10 Fletching to create the bronze darts. This step does not require the quest to be completed. 1.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per bronze dart.

label: Bronze dart tip
title: Bronze dart tip
lead:
The bronze dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players with at least 4 Smithing can smith 10 dart tips by using a bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory. They can be fletched into bronze darts at level 10 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 18 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.

label: Bronze fire arrow
title: Bronze fire arrow
lead:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same Ranged Strength as regular bronze arrows.

label: Bronze full helm
title: Bronze full helm
lead:
The bronze full helmet is the weakest full helmet in Old School RuneScape. The bronze full helmet grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart, though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic. There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

To create a bronze full helmet the player needs at least 7 Smithing, a hammer and 2 bronze bars. To make a helmet use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 Smithing experience.

label: Bronze javelin
title: Bronze javelin
lead:
The bronze javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching bronze javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 3 Fletching, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

label: Bronze key (Prince Ali Rescue)
title: Bronze key (Prince Ali Rescue)
lead:
The bronze key is made by giving a key print and a bronze bar to Osman or by using the same items on any furnace, and it is collected from Leela during Prince Ali Rescue to open the cell door to Prince Ali.

Should players lose the key, they must pay 15 coins to reclaim it from Leela.

label: Bronze kiteshield
title: Bronze kiteshield
lead: The Bronze kiteshield is the weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 12 Smithing can make the shield by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.

label: bronze knife
title: bronze knife
lead:
Bronze knives are the lowest level throwing knives available, and do not require a Ranged level to wield. They can be poisoned, and due to being one-handed, can be wielded alongside a shield.

Bronze knives can be created from a bronze bar at level . Each bar makes 5 knives, and grants the player 12.5 Smithing experience. The knives can also be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den, requiring and .

label: Bronze longsword
title: Bronze longsword
lead: The bronze longsword is a longsword made of bronze. It is the weakest longsword available, and any player can wield it. It requires 2 bronze bars and level 6 Smithing to make, granting 25 experience. The bronze longsword is available for purchase at Varrock Swordshop in Varrock. It is rarely used due to the existence of the iron longsword, which is stronger and has the same requirements. It can be found as a drop from various monsters.

label: Bronze mace
title: Bronze mace
lead: The Bronze mace is a mace made of bronze. It is the weakest mace in the game, and can be equipped at level 1 Attack. A bronze mace can be created at level 2 Smithing using 1 bronze bar. This item spawns in Sorceress' house in southern Al Kharid, and can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.

label: Bronze med helm
