title: Bronze med helm
lead:
The bronze med helm is the weakest medium helmet. It can be equipped to give a player small Defence bonuses in combat. Players can make a bronze med helm with a Smithing level of 3 by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this medium helmet from Peksa's Helmet Shop in the Barbarian Village or in the Warrior Guild Armoury from Anton.

A bronze med helm is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests. A bronze med helm spawn exists in the south-eastern corner of Draynor Manor. Falador and Edgeville town guards wear these helms as part of their uniform; as well the Black Knights' Fortress' guards.

label: Bronze pick head
title: Bronze pick head
lead:
A bronze pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the bronze pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

label: Bronze pickaxe
title: Bronze pickaxe
lead:
A bronze pickaxe is a pickaxe made of bronze. It is given to players during the Mining part of Tutorial Island and is part of the starting gear given to the player when leaving Tutorial Island. It mines on an 8-tick cycle, making it the slowest pickaxe.

Bronze pickaxes spawn in several locations in Misthalin and Asgarnia, and they can also be bought from various shops. It can also be obtained for free from Monlum, the mining tutor, in the East Lumbridge Swamp mine. A bronze pickaxe is also given to the player by Doric when starting Doric's Quest.

label: Bronze platebody
title: Bronze platebody
lead:
The bronze platebody is an armour used in melee and the weakest of all platebodies. It has no Defence requirement to equip and provides greater protection than a bronze chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 18 Smithing can make one by using 5 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 62.5 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy or Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.

label: Bronze platelegs
title: Bronze platelegs
lead:
Bronze platelegs are leg armour made of bronze, requiring level 1 Defence to wear (as is the same with other bronze and iron items). They share the same defensive stats as a bronze plateskirt but weigh more. They can be made at level 16 Smithing by using a hammer and 3 bronze bars at an anvil.

These can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid.

label: Bronze plateskirt
title: Bronze plateskirt
lead: A bronze plateskirt is the weakest plateskirt in Old School RuneScape. It has identical stat bonuses to the bronze platelegs but weighs less. A player with 16 Smithing can make it by using three bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 smithing experience. They can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

label: Bronze scimitar
title: Bronze scimitar
lead:
The bronze scimitar is a scimitar made of bronze. The weakest scimitar in the game, it requires level 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze scimitar with level 5 Smithing using 2 bronze bars, granting 25 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this scimitar from Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid.

One can be found for free on the top floor of a house in Rimmington.

label: Bronze spear
title: Bronze spear
lead:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape. Spears are members-only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow.

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins. There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite, with a specimen brush, specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith.

label: Bronze sq shield
title: Bronze sq shield
lead: The Bronze sq shield is the lowest level defence square shield in Old School RuneScape. It can be equipped to give a player better defence bonuses in combat. Its recommended use is in melee combat. Players can make a bronze square shield with 2 bronze bars at level 8 Smithing, granting 25 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.

label: Bronze sword
title: Bronze sword
lead:
The bronze sword is a low-level weapon made of bronze. It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop, or made at level 4 Smithing using 1 bronze bar, granting 12.5 experience.

A bronze sword is given to the player by Vannaka on Tutorial Island.

label: Bronze thrownaxe
title: Bronze thrownaxe
lead: The bronze thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. There are no requirements to wield a bronze throwing axe. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The bronze throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.

label: bronze warhammer
title: bronze warhammer
lead:
A bronze warhammer is a warhammer made with 3 bronze bars, requiring 9 Smithing, yielding 37.5 Smithing experience.

It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear and Vigr's Warhammers for coins.

label: bronze wire
title: bronze wire
lead: Bronze wire can be created by players with level 4 in Smithing by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in your inventory. A total of 7 are used in quests, such as Creature of Fenkenstrain (3 required, unnoted), Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete (3 required) and Shilo Village (1 required).

label: Brother Brace
title: Brother Brace
lead: Brother Brace is a Saradominist monk on Tutorial Island who teaches players how to use Prayer. Players can find him in the chapel on Tutorial Island.

label: Brother Cedric
title: Brother Cedric
lead:
Brother Cedric is a drunken monk aided during the Monk's Friend quest.

He is found standing next to his broken cart south of the Ardougne Zoo, just north of the Ardougne Monastery.

label: Brother Jered
title: Brother Jered
lead: Brother Jered is a monk at the Edgeville Monastery. Players may speak to him to have their unblessed symbol blessed one at a time. Since he is on the , only those with a Prayer level of 31 can access him. Players who achieve level 99 Prayer may purchase the Prayer cape from him for 99,000 coins.

label: Brother Kojo
title: Brother Kojo
lead:
Brother Kojo is a monk who oversees the Clock Tower. When the player first meets him, the clock has stopped working, due to the fact that the four cogs that keep the clock running have been taken; players can start the Clock Tower quest to help repair it.

He also makes watches, which the player can obtain from him if they have a sextant and a chart in their inventory. The watches can be used to solve coordinate clues.

label: Brother Omad
title: Brother Omad
lead:
Brother Omad is a monk in the Monastery south of Ardougne. Players can talk to him to start the Monk's Friend quest.

During the quest he wants you to retrieve a child's blanket. After player gives him the blanket he decides to organise a party.

label: Brown apron
title: Brown apron
lead:
Brown aprons are used to enter the Crafting Guild. They can be purchased from several clothing stores, such as Thessalia's Fine Clothes store in the centre of Varrock, for 2 coins.

A brown apron can be obtained from the Tool store 3 built in the Workshop of a player-owned house. Members can also claim them from Malignius Mortifer after the Swan Song quest.

label: Brown headband
title: Brown headband
lead: The brown headband is a members only item worn on the head. There are no requirements to wear it and it is purely cosmetic, meaning it does not offer any combat bonuses.

label: Brown toy horsey
title: Brown toy horsey
lead:
Brown toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says

label: Bucket
title: Bucket
lead:
A bucket is one of the most common items available. They can be purchased cheaply from most general stores and can also be found in many locations throughout the game. Buckets are commonly used for skills such as Crafting, Cooking and Farming.

Buckets can contain any of the following items:

label: Bucket of milk
title: Bucket of milk
lead:
A bucket of milk is a Cooking ingredient used to make a variety of drinks and foods such as choc saturdays and cakes, as well as several feeders. Players can use a bucket on a dairy cow or dairy buffalo to create a bucket of milk, or simply click on the cow or buffalo with at least one empty bucket in the inventory.

Players can turn a bucket of milk into chocolatey milk by adding chocolate dust, or add milk to nettle tea (though this does not add any effects). Depending on their Cooking level, Members can use a dairy churn to turn a bucket of milk into a pot of cream, a pat of butter, or a piece of cheese.

label: bucket of sand
title: bucket of sand
lead: A bucket of sand can be obtained by using an empty bucket with a sand pit or sand pile. They may also be obtained from Drew by mining sandstone and depositing it in the grinder next to him. They are a key component in creating molten glass, which is often used in Crafting and Construction, either via a furnace along with soda ash or by casting Superglass Make along with soda ash, seaweed or giant seaweed.

label: Bucket of water
title: Bucket of water
lead:
A bucket of water is made by using a bucket on a water source such as a fountain, a sink or a well. A bucket is the only vessel that can be filled from a well.

Like other vessels filled with water, a bucket of water has everyday uses such as transforming clay into soft clay. A bucket of water can also be used to fill a watering can.

label: bucket of wax
title: bucket of wax
lead:
A bucket of wax is obtained by interacting with a beehive in the apiary south of Seers' Village, west of Catherby. The player must have an empty bucket in their inventory, and either wear full beekeeper's outfit or use insect repellent on the beehive first. This process must be repeated per bucket of wax. It is used in the Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance quests.

There is a bucket spawn right beside the gate of the apiary.

label: Bugs
title: Bugs
lead:
Bugs is an ogre who is the son of Rantz and brother of Fycie. In Recipe for Disaster, both Bugs and his sister use the ogre boat ride to get to Karamja. Both Bugs and his sister are also featured in Big Chompy Bird Hunting when the player has to cook the Chompy bird to their liking.

Bugs also features briefly in The Corsair Curse, where the player discovers him in the water through a telescope in an attempt to debunk Cabin Boy Colin's theory of the curse affecting Captain Tock's crew. Colin mistook Bugs to be a mermaid and supposedly offended him, resulting in the belief that he was responsible for the curse.

label: Bullroarer
title: Bullroarer
lead:
The bullroarer is a quest item used during and after the Legends' Quest. During the quest, it is obtained by giving a complete map of Kharazi Jungle to a forester just outside the Kharazi Jungle. The bullroarer is used to summon a local tribesman named Gujuo from the dense jungle at various points during the quest for advice on how to proceed at each point. When used, players swing it around their heads, making a whirring sound.

Sometimes, swinging it near an oomlie bird or a tormented warrior makes them angry for disturbing the jungle's peace, whereupon they attack the player. Also, swinging it not far enough into the jungle makes nothing happen, with a message in the chat box saying, You feel a bit silly at first, but soon it makes an interesting sound. If used in an area other than the Kharazi Jungle, nothing will happen.

label: Bullrushes
title: Bullrushes
lead: Bullrushes are non-interactive scenery, typically found near the edge of water bodies across Gielinor.

label: bunny ears
title: bunny ears
lead:
Bunny ears are an untradeable cosmetic holiday item worn on the head. A pair of bunny ears can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July) as part of a rare item drop.

label: Buried skeleton (Digsite)
title: Buried skeleton (Digsite)
lead: Buried skeletons can be found within the training and level 3 digs at the Digsite. Searching the skeleton results in the player finding nothing of interest. Using a trowel on the skeleton with a Digsite workman nearby will provide dialogue of the workman telling the player off.

label: Buried skeleton (Shaman Caves)
title: Buried skeleton (Shaman Caves)
lead: A buried skeleton can be found in the room with the Carved rocks in the Shaman Caves. The skeleton can be searched, which provides a bronze pickaxe if the player is not already holding a pickaxe. The size of the skeleton and the presence of a pickaxe next to it indicates that it likely belongs to a dwarf. Additionally, the examine text says it is "probably dwarven remains", and Ungadulu says his great-grandfather told him dwarves once went down into the caves and never returned.

label: Buried skeleton (Temple of Ikov)
title: Buried skeleton (Temple of Ikov)
lead: A buried skeleton can be found in the icy area of the Temple of Ikov. Searching the skeleton results in the message Nothing interesting happens.

label: Burnt batta
title: Burnt batta
lead:
Burnt batta is the result of accidentally burning a raw batta while attempting to make a half baked batta. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt batta has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a batta tin. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt bones
title: Burnt bones
lead:
Burnt bones are one of the few bones that free players can bury to train Prayer, with the others being normal bones, big bones, and monkey bones. They can be found in the Kebos Battlefront, the Lizardman Canyon, the Dragon Nest, and various locations in the Wilderness.

Burnt bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 13.5 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 13.5 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 15.7 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.
* 18 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of burnt bonemeal.

label: Burnt bread
title: Burnt bread
lead:
Burnt bread is the result of accidentally burning bread dough while attempting to bake bread. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt bread has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt cake
title: Burnt cake
lead:
Burnt cake is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked cake while attempting to bake a cake. The burn rate will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

A burnt cake has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt chicken
title: Burnt chicken
lead:
Burnt chicken is the result of accidentally burning a raw chicken while attempting to make cooked chicken. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt chicken by cooking a piece of cooked chicken, displaying the chatbox message, You deliberately burn the nicely cooked chicken.

Burnt chicken may be used for the Forgettable Tale... quest, in which it may be one of the random items requested by the rowdy dwarf before he will give the player his Kelda seed. It is also one of the items that Gunslik and the rowdy dwarf can request when doing Keldagrim tasks.

label: Burnt crunchies
title: Burnt crunchies
lead:
Burnt crunchies is the result of accidentally burning raw crunchies while attempting to make a half baked crunchy. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt crunchies has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a crunchy tray. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt curry
title: burnt curry
lead:
Burnt curry is the result of accidentally burning uncooked curry while attempting to make curry. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

The burnt curry has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim the bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (anchovies)
title: Burnt fish (anchovies)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw anchovies while attempting to make anchovies. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (herring)
title: Burnt fish (herring)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw herring or raw mackerel. Cooking herring requires 5 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 41, and mackerel requires 10 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 45.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (sardine)
title: Burnt fish (sardine)
lead:
A burnt fish is the result of burning a raw sardine while attempting to cook a sardine. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt foods, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (trout)
title: Burnt fish (trout)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw giant carp, raw trout, raw cod, raw pike, or raw salmon. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.
* Giant carp stops being burnt at level 45.
* Trout stops being burnt at level 49.
* Cod stops being burnt at level 51.
* Pike stops being burnt at level 54.
* Salmon stops being burnt at level 58.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (tuna)
title: Burnt fish (tuna)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw tuna or raw bass. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. Tuna requires 30 Cooking to attempt to cook and stops being burnt at level 63, while bass requires 43 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 80.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt gnomebowl
title: Burnt gnomebowl
lead:
Burnt gnomebowl is the result of accidentally burning a raw gnomebowl while attempting to make a half baked bowl. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt gnomebowl has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a gnomebowl mould. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt lobster
title: Burnt lobster
lead:
Burnt lobster is the result of accidentally burning a raw lobster while attempting to make a lobster. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 64 instead.

The burnt lobster has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt manta ray
title: Burnt manta ray
lead:
Burnt manta ray is the result of accidentally burning a raw manta ray while attempting to make a manta ray. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where manta rays stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt manta ray has no use whatsoever, although you can unsuccessfully attempt to eat it. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt meat
title: Burnt meat
lead:
Burnt meat is the result of accidentally burning various raw meat while attempting to make cooked meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt meat by cooking a piece of cooked meat, displaying the chatbox message "You deliberately burn the nicely cooked meat."

Burnt meat is used for the Witch's Potion quest. It is often dropped by Imps, and is also a reward from Burntmeat after Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure.

label: burnt oomlie
title: burnt oomlie
lead:
Burnt oomlie is the result of burning a raw oomlie. This requires 50 Cooking, but unless it is wrapped in a palm leaf first, it will always be burnt.

The burnt oomlie has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt oomlie wrap
title: burnt oomlie wrap
lead: Burnt oomlie wrap is the result of accidentally burning a wrapped oomlie while attempting to make a cooked oomlie wrap. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 40 when cooking on a range and level 44 when cooking on a fire.

label: Burnt pie
title: Burnt pie
lead:
Burnt pie is the result of accidentally burning any kind of pie. The burn rate while cooking pies will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt pie has no use whatsoever, but it can be emptied to reclaim a pie dish. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt pitta bread
title: Burnt pitta bread
lead:
Burnt pitta bread is the result of accidentally burning pitta dough while attempting to make pitta bread. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 37.

However, since pitta bread cannot be made until level 58 Cooking, burnt pitta bread cannot be obtained via normal means. The method used to obtain a burnt oomlie wrap cannot be used, since using chill to drain from 58 to 36 Cooking would take longer than it takes to cook a full inventory of pitta bread. Furthermore, pitta dough can only be cooked at a range, which are not found in proximity to areas with the chill effect.

label: burnt pizza
title: burnt pizza
lead:
Burnt pizza is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked pizza while attempting to bake a pizza. The burn rate while baking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 68.

The burnt pizza has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt sea turtle
title: burnt sea turtle
lead:
Burnt sea turtle is the result of accidentally burning a raw sea turtle while attempting to make a sea turtle. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where sea turtles stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt sea turtle has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt shark
title: burnt shark
lead:
Burnt shark is the result of accidentally burning a raw shark while attempting to cook it. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 94 when wearing cooking gauntlets.

The burnt shark has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange. Because of that, some players collect them or resell them to other burnt food collectors.

label: Burnt stew
title: Burnt stew
lead:
Burnt stew is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked stew while attempting to make stew. Cooking stew requires 25 Cooking. Players will stop burning stews at level 58 Cooking.

The burnt stew has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt swordfish
title: burnt swordfish
lead:
Burnt swordfish is the result of accidentally burning a raw swordfish while attempting to make a swordfish. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 86; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 81 instead.

The burnt swordfish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burntmeat
title: Burntmeat
lead:
Burntmeat is a troll featured in Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure. He can be found in the Troll Stronghold kitchen.

Burntmeat is criticised by other trolls for only being able to cook burnt meat; however, he believes that he is a master chef. Should players help him during a quest, he rewards them with burnt meat, which he claims is very valuable.

label: Burst of Strength
title: Burst of Strength
lead:
Burst of Strength is a prayer unlocked at level 4. Burst of Strength increases the player's Strength by 5% when activated, or by 1 level if the player's Strength level is lower than 20.

Like all other stat-affecting prayers, it cannot be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Strength level, such as Superhuman Strength.

label: Burthorpe
title: Burthorpe
lead:
The Principality of Burthorpe, referred to colloquially as Burthorpe, is a military principality north-west of Falador and north of Taverley. It's led by Crown Prince Anlaf and is home to the Burthorpe Imperial Guard, who defend the citadel standing between Burthorpe and Trollheim against trolls in the ongoing Burthorpe–Troll Country War.

Burthorpe is one of the only locations in Asgarnia that isn't directly controlled by the White Knights, who many of Burthorpe's residents believe are taking advantage of Asgarnia's King, the father of Prince Anlaf.

label: Burthorpe Castle
title: Burthorpe Castle
lead: Burthorpe Castle is the central feature of the principality of Burthorpe. Various houses and businesses are lined around the castle, and its lower level contains the Burthorpe Games Room.

label: Burthorpe Supplies
title: Burthorpe Supplies
lead: Burthorpe Supplies is a general store run by Wistan in Burthorpe. Aside from the shopkeeper, the ground floor has some boxes, a bookcase, and non-interactive shelves and crates. The upper floor has crates, tables, beds, a fireplace, and some bookcases that the player can search.

label: Bush (The Dig Site)
title: Bush (The Dig Site)
lead: Many searchable bushes are found around the Digsite. One of them contains Teddy, while the rest contain nothing of interest.

label: Bush (Watchtower)
title: Bush (Watchtower)
lead: A large amount of Bushes can be found just north of the Watchtower. They can all be searched, with the majority of them containing nothing, but one contains fingernails which are used during the Watchtower quest. Four of the bushes also contain a Damaged dagger, a Tattered eye patch, an Old robe, and an Unusual armour, none of these items serve any purpose.

label: Butler Jones
title: Butler Jones
lead:
Butler Jones is the butler of the Carnillean family in East Ardougne. During the Hazeel Cult quest the player discovers that he is part of the cult of Hazeel. Should the player side with the Carnilleans against the cult, Butler Jones is arrested; if the player sides with the cultists, he remained with them to await further orders.

In Secrets of the North, should the player have sided with the Carnilleans, Jones' status becomes unknown to the cult. If they sided with the cult, Jones fled following Ceril's murder for reasons unknown, though the family guard believes that he was the prime suspect as Ceril was murdered in his room, which Hazeel found cowardly. Despite his attempts to flee, Jones is eventually apprehended by the authorities. If players sided with the cult, the guard later reveals that Jones was found dead in his cell after quest, having been killed by poison.

label: Butterfly (scenery)
title: Butterfly (scenery)
lead:
Butterflies are insects found throughout Gielinor, primarily in woodland areas.

Unlike other butterflies, they cannot be caught through Hunter. Players can command wily cats to chase them, though this does not reward anything.

label: Buttons
title: Buttons
lead: Buttons are dropped by H.A.M. Guards, thieved from H.A.M. Members in the H.A.M. Hideout behind the Lumbridge General Store, earned from the Fishing Trawler minigame, dug up at the Digsite, or obtained from Ogre Coffins. Polishing them into polished buttons requires 3 Crafting, yielding 5 Crafting experience and the message: "You rub the buttons on your clothes and they become more shiny." Polished buttons are used in the Animal Magnetism quest. Without the required Crafting level the message says: "You rub the buttons on your clothes but they aren't improved by the process."

label: Cabbage
title: Cabbage
lead:
A cabbage is a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 7 with cabbage seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten. When picking cabbages from fields, members may randomly receive 1 cabbage seed.

When eaten, the message You eat the cabbage. Yuck! is displayed. When eaten while below full health, the message It heals some health anyway. is shown as well.

label: Cabbage (Draynor Manor)
title: Cabbage (Draynor Manor)
lead:
A cabbage picked at Draynor Manor is unlike other cabbages; it appears slightly darker, and when eaten, it restores 1 Hitpoint and grants a temporary skill boost to Defence. The item cannot be traded on the Grand Exchange and can only be obtained from one of seven cabbage plants located in between the west side of the house and the fence directly north of the farming patch on the minimap.

When eaten, the messages You eat the cabbage. and It seems to taste nicer than normal. are displayed.

label: Cabbage (scenery)
title: Cabbage (scenery)
lead: Cabbage plants can be picked to obtain cabbages. Rarely, a cabbage seed is awarded in place of a cabbage. Cabbages picked in a field will respawn after 40 to 80 ticks (24 to 48 seconds) depending on world population. Unlike cabbages picked from a Farming allotment, picking cabbages from fields provides no experience.

label: Cabin Boy Jenkins
title: Cabin Boy Jenkins
lead:
Cabin Boy Jenkins is a crew member on the Lady Lumbridge, a ship that a player buys during the Dragon Slayer I quest. Despite the ship's changing hands, Jenkins continued to serve aboard.

He comes with the player and Ned when the Lady Lumbridge sets sail towards to Crandor. However, nearing the island, Elvarg swoops out of the sky and attacks the ship. He is incinerated by Elvarg's dragonfire, along with much of the ship.

label: Cadantine
title: Cadantine
lead:
Clean cadantine is a high level herb. It is used to make super defence potions at level 66 Herblore. Players can obtain it by cleaning a Grimy cadantine at level 65 Herblore, which gives 12.5 Herblore experience for cleaning.

One way to obtain cadantine herbs is through farming Cadantine seeds which requires 67 Farming.

label: Cadantine potion (unf)
title: Cadantine potion (unf)
lead: A cadantine potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a cadantine on a vial of water, requiring 66 Herblore. Using white berries on a cadantine potion (unf) with 66 Herblore yields a super defence(3) and 150 Herblore experience.

label: Cadava berries
title: Cadava berries
lead:
Cadava berries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting cadavaberry seeds or picked from wild cadava bushes. They are used as payment to protect cactus (x6).

The Apothecary in Varrock will exchange them for four-dose antipoison. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

label: Cadava potion
title: Cadava potion
lead:
The cadava potion is a quest item used in Romeo & Juliet. It is made by giving Cadava berries to the Apothecary in Varrock. The Apothecary then supposedly adds four other ingredients in order to complete the potion: "Wing of rat, tail of frog. Ear of snake and horn of dog."

The cadava potion is used to fake Juliet's death so Romeo can meet her.

label: Cairn Isle
title: Cairn Isle
lead:
Cairn Isle is an island on the south-west of Karamja, south of Tai Bwo Wannai and west of Shilo Village. To access the island, players must scale a small promontory stood on the Karamjan coastline by climbing up a rockslide (requires 15 Agility), and then walk across the wooden bridge linking up the two islands. In case the player stumbles while climbing the rockslide, they will slide back down and take damage. If the player fails to keep their balance while crossing the bridge, they will fall off and be washed back to the shoreline of Karamja, again taking damage. It is advised to bring food if determined to make it to the island.

The chance of successfully crossing the bridge to Cairn Isle is dependent on the player's Agility level, scaling up to a 98% chance at a safe passage at level 99. Whether the player walks or runs across the bridges does not influence this skill check.

label: Cake
title: Cake
lead:
Cake is a type of food that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 4. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked cake on a cooking range, requiring level 40 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt cake. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

Stealing a cake from the Ardougne Baker's Stall. is an easy Ardougne Diary task.

label: Cake tin
title: Cake tin
lead:
A cake tin is an item used to bake cakes. Players need to add an egg, a pot of flour and a bucket of milk on to the cake tin and used in an oven.

They can be found in the Cooks' Guild, bought from any general store (except for the ones in Port Phasmatys, Ardougne, Port Khazard, Canifis, Keldagrim, and Burthorpe), bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest in Lumbridge, or taken from the wooden shelves from a player-owned house. The cake tin also respawns at the house with an anvil in the level 21 Wilderness.

label: Caleb
title: Caleb
lead:
Caleb Fitzharmon is a cook that lives north of Catherby bank, and plays a part in the Family Crest quest. Caleb has two brothers, Avan and Johnathon, who also feature in the quest. He is the oldest son of Dimintheis Fitzharmon.

After the quest, he will enchant a player's steel gauntlets into cooking gauntlets for free, provided the gauntlets have never been enchanted before. If they have however, he will charge 25,000 coins each time thereafter. If the Family Pest miniquest has been completed, Caleb will give the cooking gauntlets directly for free instead.

label: camel
title: camel
lead:
A camel is a type of creature that inhabits the Kharidian Desert. These include dromedary camels (Camelus dromedarius), which have one hump, Bactrian camels (C. bactrianus), which have two humps, and Ugthanki (C. horribleus).

Camels can be found in Al Kharid, Ardougne Zoo, and the Bedabin Camp.

label: Camelot
title: Camelot
lead:
The Castle of Camelot is a stone's throw east from the famous city of Seers' Village. Home to King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table, the castle is also the starting point for the Holy Grail and Merlin's Crystal quests. The Camelot Castle might also be a frequent venture for players following clue scrolls.

Camelot was once the home of the Sinclair family. However, when the Knights of the Round Table came to Gielinor, Lord Sinclair gave the castle to them and moved to another place known as Sinclair Mansion.

label: Camelot (music track)
title: Camelot (music track)
lead: Camelot is a music track that is unlocked inside the gates of Camelot Castle, or in Classic mode it can be unlocked at the very western part of Tenzing's garden and on Mac's island. It can also be heard in the jail during King's Ransom.

label: Camelot Teleport
title: Camelot Teleport
lead:
Camelot Teleport teleports the caster to the front gate of Camelot. Camelot Teleport is an excellent training spell, because you can use an air staff and use up only one law rune per cast for extremely quick and easy experience. It is possible to earn upwards of 80,000 Magic experience an hour with this method of training, however most players switch to using High Level Alchemy when 55 Magic is achieved.

Casting this spell is a requirement for the medium Kandarin diary. After completing the Kandarin Hard tasks, you may switch the location of the teleport to Seers' Village bank by right-clicking the spell and choosing Toggle-location.

label: Campsite bed
title: Campsite bed
lead: Campsite beds are found in several camps all around Gielinor. Players cannot interact with the beds, but they can examine them.

label: Candle
title: Candle
lead:
A candle is the lowest tier of Firemaking light sources. It can be lit with a tinderbox. Lit candles can be extinguished by clicking extinguish on them or falling into swamp water in the Lumbridge Caves. Candles may be acquired through various means such as finding them within certain houses, purchasing them from a candle seller or candle maker, or by trading with other players.

A candle is a required item for Enlightened Journey and Enakhra's Lament.

label: candle maker
title: candle maker
lead: The candle maker can be found in his Candle Shop in Catherby. He sells candles for three coins each. During Merlin's Crystal, the player must give a bucket of wax to the candle-maker, and he will make a black candle for the player. Although he considers black candles unlucky, he will continue selling them for three coins each.

label: Candle Shop
title: Candle Shop
lead: The Candle Shop, as the name implies, only sells candles. It is owned by the Candle maker and located in Catherby, just a little west of the town's bank. Players who need a black candle for the Merlin's Crystal quest can get one by trading a bucket of wax to this shop.

label: Canifis
title: Canifis
lead: Canifis, formerly known as Kharyrll, is a small town in Morytania inhabited by werewolves in human form. The town is only accessible to players who have completed the Priest in Peril quest. Canifis is the starting point for the Myreque storyline.

label: Canifis bank
title: Canifis bank
lead: The Canifis bank is a bank located in Canifis. The bank can be quickly accessed via the Kharyrll Teleport spell. Players often use the bank when completing tasks at the Slayer Tower, as well as to safespot the werewolves on the bank's table.

label: Cannon barrels
title: Cannon barrels
lead: Cannon barrels are the third part of the dwarf multicannon set up on top of the cannon base after placing the cannon stand and before the cannon furnace. They shoot the enemy with a barrage of steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for coins.

label: Cannon base
title: Cannon base
lead:
The cannon base is the first part of the dwarf multicannon to be set up, followed by the stand. The Dwarf Cannon quest must be completed to use it. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for coins.

The cannon base by itself can decay without having the full cannon set up. When lost, a new cannon base can be obtained from Nulodion, free of charge.

label: Cannon furnace
title: Cannon furnace
lead: The cannon furnace powers the dwarf multicannon. It is the last part to be setup after the cannon barrels. Once setup, 30 steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs can be loaded for the dwarf multicannon to fire. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for coins.

label: Cannon stand
title: Cannon stand
lead: The cannon stand is the second part of the dwarf multicannon set up on the ground after the cannon base and before cannon barrels. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for coins.

label: Cap'n Izzy No-Beard
title: Cap'n Izzy No-Beard
lead:
Cap'n Izzy No-Beard is a pirate captain and master of Agility who can be found at the entrance of the Brimhaven Agility Arena minigame. He has a pet parrot which he says has "cracked Jenny's tea cup." He and his parrot guard the entrance to the Agility arena, with an entry fee of 200 coins to use the arena. Upon paying the entrance fee, the message You give Cap'n Izzy the 200 coin entrance fee. will be displayed.

As master of Agility, players with level 99 Agility may purchase an Agility cape from him for 99,000 coins. As with all skillcapes, it also comes with the matching skillcape hood.

label: Cape of legends
title: Cape of legends
lead:
The cape of legends is a cape that can be bought for from Siegfried Erkle at the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items on the western portion of the of the Legends' Guild. They can also purchase it from Perdu for should they lose it after purchasing it at least once. Like the obsidian cape, it has balanced defence bonuses, but has 2 less in each stat while also being much cheaper.

As the Guild's interior can only be accessed upon completion of the Legends' Quest, this cape can only be owned by those that have completed said quest and became a member of the Guild. There are various NPCs who appear to be wearing the cape or some variation thereof. (See [[#Trivia|Trivia]])

label: Captain Barnaby
title: Captain Barnaby
lead:
Captain Barnaby is an old sea captain who takes players between East Ardougne, Brimhaven, and Rimmington by his ship. His toll is 30 coins, similar to all other ships to and from Karamja.

This toll can be reduced to 15 coins by wearing any form of Karamja gloves, obtained from the Karamja Diary. Going through his dialogue with a Ring of charos(a) equipped will make the trip there and back free, not through the pay-fare option.

label: Captain Lawgof
title: Captain Lawgof
lead:
Captain Lawgof is the captain of the Dwarven Black Guard who is in charge of the Coal Trucks west of Seers' Village. Members can speak to him to start the Dwarf Cannon quest.

He is quite frustrated about the goblins that attack his base and try to overwhelm his defences and will gladly look for an adventurer to help him.

label: Captain Rovin
title: Captain Rovin
lead:
Captain Milo Rovin is a prominent captain of the Varrock guard. He takes his job very seriously, questioning players for entering restricted areas. Players can also choose to tell him about the castle's ale delivery, in which case he will direct them to the kitchen staff.

The captain can be found on the of the north-west tower of the castle, at the top of a spiral staircase. He plays a role in the Demon Slayer quest, holding one of the keys to Silverlight's case.

label: Captain Shanks
title: Captain Shanks
lead:
Captain Shanks is the captain of the Lady of the Waves and plays a small role during the One Small Favour quest. He will take players on a one way trip to Port Khazard or Port Sarim, provided they have purchased a ship ticket from Seravel.

He is one of three NPCs in the quest not to ask a favour (he does not do favours). The second is Gnormadium Avlafrim, who does not ask because he does not think you are capable of doing it. The third is Fred the Farmer who cannot fulfil your favour due to a lack of chickens and tells you to go talk to Seth Groats instead.

label: Captain Siad
title: Captain Siad
lead:
Captain Siad is the man who controls the Desert Mining Camp, a harsh camp deep in the Kharidian Desert that takes prisoners from Al Kharid and has them work as slaves in the mines. Players must investigate Siad's room during The Tourist Trap, though he watches the player and distrusts them. However, once the player searches his bookcases and finds that he has an interest in sailing, they can distract him while he talks about his days at sea and find the Wrought iron key and the Cell door key. Sure enough, if a player searches the bookcase in his office, they will find the Sailing book.

After completion of the quest and with 50 Sailing, the player can return to Siad to recruit him as a crewmate. Siad will gladly take up the offer and abandon his post, becoming Ex-Captain Siad. The Metal key (or steel key ring if you've added the key to it) is required to access the camp again. You can kill the Mercenary Captain outside the gate entrance to obtain another key, so long as the key is not in your bank or on your steel key ring. Unequip your weapon and armour before entering the camp.

label: Captain Tobias
title: Captain Tobias
lead:
Captain Tobias is a sailor found in Port Sarim. Along with Seaman Thresnor and Seaman Lorris, players can ask him to take them to Musa Point in Karamja or The Pandemonium at a cost of 30 coins.

The cost for travel to Musa Point is reduced to 15 coins while wearing any form of Karamja gloves. If the player is wearing a ring of charos (a), they need not pay anything.

label: Carla
title: Carla
lead:
Carla is a woman in West Ardougne who is upset that she lost her son to the mourners. She claims that it seemed more like the common cold rather than a horrible disease that is affecting the city, and that it is made into such a big issue by its neighbouring city, East Ardougne.

Carla is one of the few people who suspect that the plague is a big hoax (Carla is right, as seen at the end of Biohazard, that there is no plague after all). One way to tell her apart is that she wears a bright purple dress which stands out from the drab, brown clothing worn by the rest of West Ardougne.

label: Carnillean armour
title: Carnillean armour
lead: Carnillean armour is obtainable only during Ceril's side of the Hazeel Cult quest by killing Alomone and looting the nearby chest. It is possible to get multiple armour pieces by looting the chest multiple times. Carnillean requires a Defence level of 1 to wear but has lower defensive bonuses than the iron platebody. Some mages or archers may wish to use Carnillean armour due to it not lowering magic or ranged attacks. This piece of armour will not interfere with Ava's devices.

label: Carnillean Mansion
title: Carnillean Mansion
lead:
The Carnillean Mansion is a residence located in the south
west corner of East Ardougne. The house is owned by the affluent Carnillean family, including Ceril Carnillean, Henryeta, and their son Philipe. The mansion also houses their staff, which includes Claus the chef, Butler Jones, and a guard.

The house is the starting point of the quests Hazeel Cult and Secrets of the North.

label: Carol
title: Carol
lead:
Carol Sinclair is one of Lord Sinclair's children. She is a suspect during the Murder Mystery quest.

According to the Gossip, she got conned out of a lot of money by purchasing a box full of beans from a travelling salesman who told her they were magical. In order to cover her debts, she has taken some rare books from the Mansion's library to sell.

label: Carol's barrel
title: Carol's barrel
lead: Carol's barrel can be found inside the Sinclair Mansion in Carol's bedroom. During the Murder Mystery quest, the player must search the barrel to find her silver bottle.

label: Carol's print
title: Carol's print
lead: Carol's print is a quest item in the Murder Mystery quest. It is created by using flypaper on the silver bottle after dusting it with a pot of flour. If the prints match those of the unknown print, it will become a killer's print, meaning Carol is the killer.

label: Caroline
title: Caroline
lead: Caroline starts the Sea Slug quest. She lives in a house in Witchaven, where her husband Kent and son Kennith are the only ones not being possessed by sea slugs.

label: Carrallanger
title: Carrallanger
lead: Carrallanger (also spelled “Carrallangar” or “Carrallagar” in some sources), was a Zarosian fortress that was located in current-day Wilderness. It was destroyed during the Third Age when Zaros's settlements were being wiped out by followers of Zamorak and Saradomin.

label: carved doors
title: carved doors
lead: Carved doors are scenery objects used as the entrance to Rashiliyia's Tomb that can be found north-west of the Ship Yard on Karamja. Players first must search a palm tree during the Shilo Village quest in order for the doors to appear. A bone key must then be used to open the doors, after which players may enter the hillside entrance.

label: Carved rock
title: Carved rock
lead:
The Carved rocks are stalagmites found in the Shaman Caves during the Legends' Quest. To progress further in the quest, the player must use various cut gems on the correct rocks, resulting in the binding book appearing. Placing the wrong gem on the incorrect rock will result in nothing happening and receiving the message, "You carefully move the gem closer to the rock. But nothing happens." It should also be noted that searching the rocks will make the gem appear had the player placed one, correctly. The gem can be picked-up; however, if it is picked up while it despawns the player will not receive the gem (in otherwords, it gets deleted) and the game will think the player took the gem. Essentially, a new gem will be needed to complete the puzzle. Additionally, should the player try to telekinetic grab the placed the gem, no runes will be used and the game will yield the message, "The spell fizzles and dies for some unknown reason."

Upon completing the puzzle a light show will occur to uncover the binding book. It should be noted that although the gems appear during the light show, they are unable to be picked up and attempting to do so will insert the following message into the player's chat box, "The gem seems untouchable, as if it wasn't even there."

label: casket
title: casket
lead: A casket is an item occasionally dropped by NPCs and monsters that are near oceans or bodies of water. It can also be obtained via big net fishing, at a rate of about 1/128 at lower levels and 1/85.3 at higher levels. The fishing spot in Civitas illa Fortis has around a 1 in 5 chance of rewarding a casket, making this one of the most reliable places to obtain them. It can be opened to receive a small amount of treasure. Wearing a skills necklace with at least one charge while big net fishing will slightly increase the chance of finding a casket.

label: Casket (discontinued)
title: Casket (discontinued)
lead:
A casket could previously be received after completing any step of a Treasure Trail. These caskets did not always contain a reward, and sometimes only gave another clue scroll.

On 28 July 2016 Treasure Trails were updated. Caskets were replaced with new items called Reward caskets. They are only received once all steps have been completed, and are guaranteed to contain a reward.

label: Cassie
title: Cassie
lead: Cassie is the owner of Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.

label: Cassie's Shield Shop.
title: Cassie's Shield Shop.
lead:
Cassie's Shield Shop is a specialty shop owned by Cassie that sells shields. It is located in Falador, just west of the park and south-east of the northern gate of the city.

Upstairs is a cooked chicken that respawns on the desk.

label: Cat
title: Cat
lead:
Cats are common pets that can follow the player. In order to obtain a pet cat, a player must complete the Gertrude's Cat quest, after which Gertrude will give them a kitten as part of the reward. After three hours, the kitten will grow into a pet cat. Cats no longer need the food nor attention required of a kitten, and will not run away.

After another five to six hours of having the adult cat following the player, it will become an overgrown cat. Overgrown cats can be trained into wily cats, that will eventually become lazy cats. Lazy cats can repeatedly be trained back into wily cats.

label: Cat training medal
title: Cat training medal
lead:
A cat training medal is an item worn in the neck slot that members can obtain by having their cat or kitten catch 100 rats, and then talking to Gertrude in Varrock. Hell-rats are included in this count, as well as hell-rat behemoths. This item has no effect when worn, and is purely cosmetic. If players lose or drop their training medal, they may talk to Gertrude to get another one. It is not tradeable on the Grand Exchange, but it can be traded in person with other players.

Kittens have a low chance of catching rats, so it is recommended to wait until your kitten has grown into a cat before you try to catch rats. The cat must catch the rats before it turns into an overgrown cat, which cannot hunt vermin. Players who only have overgrown cats must buy another kitten from Gertrude (or wait for it to become lazy). Note that wily cats are not eligible for a medal, and training an overgrown cat into a wily cat also resets the rat kill counter to zero even after it becomes lazy. Receiving a new kitten from Gertrude will also reset the counter, as will letting a cat mature into an overgrown one.

label: Catherby
title: Catherby
lead:
Catherby is a small fishing town located south-east of Camelot and west of White Wolf Mountain. It is a members-only town with vast variety of fishing spots available on its shores for all levels of Fishing. It is also a popular town for woodcutters due to the vast amount of trees to the west of the town.

To the east of Catherby is White Wolf Mountain. This area can be deadly to low-level players as level 25 and 38 aggressive white wolves inhabit this area. To the west of Catherby is Camelot and Seers' Village, and to the south-west is the mighty city of East Ardougne, the capital of Kandarin.

label: Catherby bank
title: Catherby bank
lead:
The Catherby bank is a bank in the town of Catherby, found west of Ice Mountain. The Catherby bank was the first bank to be released to members only.

Interestingly, the bank has no doors in the back for the tellers to enter; additionally, the easternmost booth is unusable due to being blocked by a bank table.

label: cattleprod
title: cattleprod
lead:
The cattleprod is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It can be found next to the incinerator in the fenced off pen north of East Ardougne.

It is used to prod sick-looking sheep in order to move them from their habitats into the pen to be incinerated.

label: Cauldron
title: Cauldron
lead: Several cauldrons can be found in Gielinor. Most cauldrons are next to characters that are proficient in magic, and some are near non-magical characters such as soldiers. These cauldrons cannot be interacted with, only examined.

label: cauldron (Mourner Headquarters)
title: cauldron (Mourner Headquarters)
lead:
A Cauldron can be found in the garden of the Mourner Headquarters. During the Biohazard quest, a rotten apple is thrown in the cauldron to make the Mourners sick such that an adventurer can sneak into their headquarters disguised as a doctor.

During the quest, players can Inspect the cauldron, which will give some information.

label: Cauldron (Witch's Potion)
title: Cauldron (Witch's Potion)
lead:
A cauldron can be found in Hetty's house in Rimmington. At the end of Witch's Potion, the player must Drink From the cauldron. This prints the message "You drink from the cauldron. It tastes horrible! You feel yourself imbued with power.", followed by the completion of the quest.

Attempting to drink the potion when not completing the quest will cause the player to say "As nice as that looks, I think I'll give it a miss for now."

label: Cauldron of Thunder
title: Cauldron of Thunder
lead:
The Cauldron of Thunder is a special cauldron that is used in Druidic Ritual. Players need to dip raw chicken, raw beef, raw rat meat and raw bear meat into it. It is located in Taverley Dungeon, just north-east of the entrance ladder.

The cauldron is guarded by two level 19 Suits of armour that are right outside the gate. Between the cauldron and the entrance are level 22 skeletons. Players with lower combat levels should be aware of this.

label: Cave Background
title: Cave Background
lead: Cave Background is a music track that is unlocked throughout the Dwarven Mine. It can also be heard in the Magic axe room of Taverley Dungeon.

label: Cave entrance (Ardougne to Underground Pass)
title: Cave entrance (Ardougne to Underground Pass)
lead: A cave entrance is used to enter the Underground Pass from West Ardougne. It is located on the western edge of West Ardougne. Players must enter the Underground Pass during the Underground Pass quest.

label: Cave entrance (Clivet)
title: Cave entrance (Clivet)
lead: Cave entrance is the entrance to the Ardougne Sewers, south of East Ardougne. Players must visit the sewers to speak with Clivet during Hazeel Cult.

label: Cave Entrance (Eadgar's cave)
title: Cave Entrance (Eadgar's cave)
lead: A Cave Entrance is used to enter Eadgar's cave on the top of Trollheim. It is easily accessed by running just south of the Trollheim Teleport. The cave is visited during the Troll Stronghold and Eadgar's Ruse quests.

label: Cave entrance (from Ogre Enclave)
title: Cave entrance (from Ogre Enclave)
lead: A cave entrance is located on the northern side of the Ogre Enclave. It is used to leave the enclave to the northern side of Gu'Tanoth.

label: Cave entrance (from Shaman Caves)
title: Cave entrance (from Shaman Caves)
lead: A cave entrance is used to exit the Shaman Caves. It is located next to the ring of fire that Ungadulu resides in. Walking through it will place the player outside near the mossy rock used to enter.

label: Cave Entrance (Goblin Cave)
title: Cave Entrance (Goblin Cave)
lead:
A Cave Entrance north of East Ardougne is the entrance to the Goblin Cave.

The Goblin Cave is entered during various quests and miniquests:

label: Cave entrance (Rantz's cave)
title: Cave entrance (Rantz's cave)
lead: A cave entrance is used to enter the Rantz's cave. It's located in the eastern part of the Feldip Hills, north-east of the fairy ring (code ). The cave is featured in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

label: Cave Entrance (Saba's cave)
title: Cave Entrance (Saba's cave)
lead: A Cave Entrance is used to enter the cave of Saba during the Death Plateau quest. It can be found north-west of Burthorpe, directly north of the Warriors' Guild and directly south of Death Plateau.

label: Cave entrance (Skavid caves)
title: Cave entrance (Skavid caves)
lead:
Cave Entrances are found around Gu'Tanoth and lead to the Skavid caves. A light source and a skavid map is needed to enter any of the caves.

If players attempt to enter a Skavid cave without having a Skavid map in their inventory, they become confused and end up outside another Skavid cave. The text then appears: "There's no way I can find my way through without a map of some kind."

label: Cave entrance (to Ogre Enclave)
title: Cave entrance (to Ogre Enclave)
lead: A cave entrance is used to enter the Ogre Enclave. It can be found on the west side of Gu'Tanoth to the west of the ogre traders. A cave nightshade is needed to access the cave during the Watchtower Quest. If returning to the cave after the quest is completed a cave nightshade is not needed.

label: Cave entrance (Toban's island)
title: Cave entrance (Toban's island)
lead: A Cave entrance can be found in north-eastern Feldip Hills. Players can use it to visit the island where Toban lives.

label: Cave Entrance (Troll Arena tunnel)
title: Cave Entrance (Troll Arena tunnel)
lead: A Cave Entrance is used to enter a small tunnel connecting Trollheim to the Troll Arena. There are two locations of the cave entrance on the north and south exterior of the tunnel.

label: Cave Exit (Eadgar's cave)
title: Cave Exit (Eadgar's cave)
lead: A Cave Exit can be found in Eadgar's cave. Players can use it to exit the cave and return to the top of Trollheim. The cave is visited during the Troll Stronghold and Eadgar's Ruse quests.

label: Cave exit (Rantz's cave)
title: Cave exit (Rantz's cave)
lead: A Cave exit is used to exit Rantz's Cave. It leads back to the eastern part of the Feldip Hills.

label: Cave Exit (Saba's cave)
title: Cave Exit (Saba's cave)
lead: A cave exit is used to exit Saba's cave during the Death Plateau quest. It leads back outside to the Death Plateau.

label: Cave exit (Skavid caves)
title: Cave exit (Skavid caves)
lead: Cave exits are found in the skavid caves and lead back to Gu'Tanoth.

label: Cave Exit (Troll Arena tunnel)
title: Cave Exit (Troll Arena tunnel)
lead: A Cave Exit can be found in the Troll Arena tunnel. Players can use it to enter Troll Country.

label: Cave exit (Underground Pass to Ardougne)
title: Cave exit (Underground Pass to Ardougne)
lead: A cave exit is used to leave the Underground Pass to West Ardougne. It is located in the north-westen side of the Underground Pass.

label: Cave in
title: Cave in
lead: The Cave in is a pile of rubble hiding the passage between the two different areas in Ah Za Rhoon during the Shilo Village quest. Searching the rubble will let the player crawl between the areas.

label: Cave monk
title: Cave monk
lead:
The cave monk is a non-player character outside of Entrana Dungeon. His only purpose is to warn players of the dangers below the island, which include zombies and greater demons, inability to use prayers, and inability to exit through the ladder back to the surface. To exit the dungeon, players must use teleportation or the magic door inside the dungeon which teleports them to high-levelled Wilderness.

The cave monk and Entrana Dungeon are involved in two quests, Lost City and Recipe for Disaster. In both, players are required to get branches off of the Dramen tree.

label: cave nightshade
title: cave nightshade
lead:
Cave nightshade, also known as cave belladonna, is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite.

Players can eat nightshade, but this is not recommended in most situations. When eaten, the player will say, "Ahhhh! What have I done!" and take up to 15 damage (damage taken scales with the player's current Hitpoints). Like most self-damaging items, it is impossible for the player to kill themselves with it. (Note: It is possible for players to eat this without losing health; if the player were to accidentally eat the nightshade, they can teleport away to avoid losing any hitpoints, provided they don't click "Continue" on the dialogue text.)

label: Cave rocks
title: Cave rocks
lead: Cave rocks are a decorative scenery element found within various underground areas. Despite having the same shape as other mineral rocks, these can not be mined.

label: Cave web
title: Cave web
lead: Cave webs are examinable scenery in the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

label: Cavern
title: Cavern
lead: Cavern is a music track that is unlocked at the Yanille Agility Dungeon and the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

label: Cell door key
title: Cell door key
lead:
Cell door key is found during the Tourist Trap quest by searching the table in the building found in north part of the Desert Mining Camp. It is useful for getting out of the jail, although it is still possible to fit through the bars and escape without it. Upon completing the quest, if needed, one can reobtain the key.

The key cannot be placed in the steel key ring.

label: cell key 1
title: cell key 1
lead:
The cell key 1 is a quest item used in the Troll Stronghold quest. It opens the cell where Godric is held. The key is held by Twig, a level 71 troll, who is sleeping while on guard in Troll Stronghold. It can be pickpocketed from him if player has level 30 Thieving, if not, players must fight him to get it.

Trying to reuse duplicates of the key after the quest will give the message, "You have no need to do this."

label: Cell key 2
title: Cell key 2
lead:
The cell key 2 is a quest item only used in the Troll Stronghold quest. It opens the cell where Eadgar is held. The key is held by Berry, a level 71 troll sleeping in guard in Troll Stronghold. It can be pickpocketed from him if player has level 30 Thieving, if not, players must fight him to get it.

Trying to reuse duplicates of the key after the quest will give the message, "You have no need to do this."

label: Cellar Song
title: Cellar Song
lead: Cellar Song is a music track that is unlocked at the vault of the Varrock West Bank and the Clan Cup lobby.

label: Ceolburg
title: Ceolburg
lead: Ceolburg is a citizen of Burthorpe who will tell you a little of what is going on in the town.

label: Ceramic remains
title: Ceramic remains
lead: Ceramic remains can be found at the Digsite. When shown to Terry Balando, he says "Yes, many parts are discovered. The inhabitants of these parts were great potters." There are currently no uses for the ceramic remains. It is considered a useless item because it can't be traded, gives no coins when alchemised, and can't be used in any way.

label: Ceril Carnillean
title: Ceril Carnillean
lead:
Sir Ceril Carnillean is part of the Carnillean family whose ancestors destroyed Hazeel, a follower of Zamorak and Mahjarrat, many years ago. In the Hazeel Cult quest, members can decide either to protect the Carnillean family or to help summon Hazeel once more.

Ceril is killed by an assassin during the events of Secrets of the North.

label: Certificate (Death Plateau)
title: Certificate (Death Plateau)
lead:
The certificate is a quest item used in the Death Plateau quest, given to players by Denulth so that Dunstan's son can join the Imperial Guard. In return, Dunstan will make players a set of spiked boots to give to Tenzing. At least one free inventory space is required to claim it.

Player who talk to Denulth with a full inventory will receive an in-game message saying Denulth has given you a certificate.. However, when asking Dunstan to make the spiked boots, he won't take the player's word. Dunstan will not make the boots unless players have a certificate in their inventory.

label: Certificate (Shield of Arrav)
title: Certificate (Shield of Arrav)
lead:
The Certificate is obtained during the Shield of Arrav quest by combining the two half certificates. Both halves of the certificate are obtained from Curator Haig Halen. However, a player can only obtain one half. The other half is obtained from a player from the opposite gang.

The quest completes when the certificate is brought to King Roald, rewarding 600 coins.

label: Chadwell
title: Chadwell
lead: Chadwell is a shopkeeper who runs the West Ardougne General Store. The store, which is one of the few stores still operating in the city of West Ardougne, is located in the south-western corner of the city, and Chadwell sells almost all of the supplies and apparel needed when going through the Underground Pass, which may be useful if the player forgets something they need. He also sells different kinds of food which can be used to heal any lost Hitpoints in the pass.

label: Chain of Command
title: Chain of Command
lead: Chain of Command is a music track that is unlocked in the Temple of Ikov.

label: Chair (Draynor Manor)
title: Chair (Draynor Manor)
lead:
Chairs are located throughout the inside of Draynor Manor, with many of them presumably being possessed. The taller chairs are recoloured variants of the spooky chair, having cobwebs spread across the back and between the legs. All the others resemble the standard chair, though much darker in colour.

The cobwebbed chairs and those in the basement do not move, but every 170 ticks (1m42s), the spinning variant will rise into the air and spin around multiple times before returning to the floor and falling still.

label: Chaise lounge
title: Chaise lounge
lead: Chaise lounges can be found in towns throughout the Kharidian Desert. Al Kharid has one near Ali the Tailor and one on the of the Al Kharid General Store. Pollnivneach has two in the building south of Ali the Operator.

label: Chalice of Eternity
title: Chalice of Eternity
lead:
The Chalice of Eternity is found in the northernmost cavern inside the Waterfall Dungeon. It is used during the climax of Waterfall Quest.

Players who attempt to "Take treasure" without following the proper procedure in the quest will be washed out of the cavern. They will also lose Glarial's amulet and Glarial's urn.

label: Challenge scroll
title: Challenge scroll
lead:
Challenge scrolls are riddles given to players by an NPC during a Treasure Trail. Challenge scrolls appear in medium, hard, and elite clue steps. Players must solve the challenge scroll in order to advance in their Treasure Trail. The challenge scroll is not a separate step in the Treasure Trail.

The questions for the challenge scrolls are always the same. Players do not have to read the challenge scroll in order to answer the question. Players only need to talk to the NPC again after receiving the scroll to answer the answer. There are no penalties for incorrect answers.

label: chamber guardian
title: chamber guardian
lead:
The Chamber guardian is found in the small cave section of the Mage Arena. He operates the Mage Arena Staffs store that sells god staves for 80,000 coins. To reach him, players need to jump into the sparkling pool.

After players have completed the Mage Arena minigame, they are rewarded with either a Saradomin staff, Guthix staff or Zamorak staff by the chamber guardian, depending on which god cape players chose. Note that he does not buy god staves back from players.

label: Champions' Guild
title: Champions' Guild
lead: The Champions' Guild is located south of Varrock and is accessible to players with at least 32 quest points. It has Scavvo's Rune Store and Valaine's Shop of Champions, and is also the starting point of the free-to-play quest, Dragon Slayer I.

label: Chancellor Hassan
title: Chancellor Hassan
lead: Chancellor Hassan is in the southern room of the ground floor of Al Kharid palace. He is the chancellor to the desert nation of Al Kharid, a large city on the northernmost fringe of the vast Kharidian Desert. Hassan is currently the acting ruler of Al Kharid in place of the Emir. He is also the start and ending points for the Prince Ali Rescue quest.

label: Chancy
title: Chancy
lead:
Chancy is one of the three individuals who agree to smuggle dangerous chemicals into Varrock during the Biohazard quest. His name is derived from his gambling addiction, gambling being based upon chance. During Biohazard, you must give him the liquid honey.

Prior to the quest, Chancy can only be found near the Chemist's house in Rimmington, practicing with a deck of cards. After the quest, he can be found in both Rimmington and the Dancing Donkey Inn in Varrock, where he is waiting to meet his gambling buddies. He is always accompanied by his associates Hops and Da Vinci.

label: Chandelier (Black Knights' Base)
title: Chandelier (Black Knights' Base)
lead: Chandelier is a scenery object located in the Black Knights' Base. Players cannot interact with the chandelier, but they can examine it.

label: chaos altar
title: chaos altar
lead:
The Chaos Altar is a runic altar upon which chaos runes are crafted from pure essence, providing 8.5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Players can also use a chaos core to craft chaos runes, which provide 85 Runecraft experience per core. Level 35 Runecraft is required to craft chaos runes.

Players may create a chaos tiara here by using either a chaos talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 37.5 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 42.5 Runecraft experience.

label: Chaos altar (Prayer)
title: Chaos altar (Prayer)
lead:
Chaos altars are altars devoted to Zamorak found in several Chaos Temples and other eerie locations across Gielinor. You can recharge your prayer points at these altars.

Praying at the chaos altar in the Yanille Agility dungeon opens a trapdoor, damaging the player and dropping them to the lower level of the dungeon where poison spiders reside.

label: chaos druid
title: chaos druid
lead:
Chaos druids are low-level humans commonly killed for their frequent drops of herbs. Unlike other druids, they worship Zamorak. They attack with their fists and make use of a spell that appears to be a combination of the Confuse and Bind spells, binding their target very briefly if successful.

Players who decide to kill chaos druids in the Edgeville Dungeon should beware of player killers who disguise themselves in Zamorak robes to take on the appearance of a chaos druid. If you attack another player, you will become skulled and potentially lose all of your items.

label: Chaos Druid Tower
title: Chaos Druid Tower
lead:
The Chaos Druid Tower is located to the north of Ardougne and is home to 4 chaos druids, located on the . The door is locked, requiring level 46 Thieving to open, and granting 37.5 experience when successful. Picking the lock does not require a lockpick.

The tower also houses the entrance to a dungeon containing two chests requiring level 59 Thieving to open. Upon doing so the player receives two blood runes and 500 coins and is granted 250 experience. Once a player has successfully opened the chest and removed its contents they will be teleported, along with their loot, to a house in the north of East Ardougne. The chest respawns every 210 seconds or 3 and a half minutes. The dungeon itself is also inhabited by 5 giant bats and 7 ogres.

label: Chaos druid warrior
title: Chaos druid warrior
lead:
Chaos druid warriors are a more powerful version of chaos druids which can be found in the Yanille Agility Dungeon (40 Agility required) or on the roof of the Slepe church. They drop more ingredients than their lower-level counterparts, and their frequent herb drops make them useful for players seeking to train Herblore.

Both locations feature an altar, but players training should be aware that praying at the chaos altar in the Yanille dungeon drops the player into a pit of level 64 poison spiders, dealing up to 15 damage.

label: Chaos dwarf
title: Chaos dwarf
lead:
Chaos dwarves are a type of corrupted and dangerous dwarves following Zamorak found in various locations, most notably the Wilderness. It is revealed during the Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf quest that they are the result of experiments by The Red Axe in their attempt to conquer Keldagrim.

On occasion, they may drop a muddy key, which can be used to unlock the muddy chest deep in the Wilderness, which contains an assortment of mid-level items. Both the dwarves in the Wilderness and those in Taverley Dungeon drop the muddy key.

label: Chaos gauntlets
title: Chaos gauntlets
lead:
Chaos gauntlets are a pair of gloves available after completing the Family Crest quest. The gauntlets, when worn, increase the maximum damage done by all bolt spells by 3 (before the boosted damage is multiplied by Magic Damage stats), thus making the max hit of bolt spells only 1 below that of blast spells and Inferior Demonbane. There are no requirements to wear these gloves.

These gloves can first be obtained by bringing steel gauntlets to Johnathon, one of the sons in the Family Crest quest. Johnathon is located upstairs in the Jolly Boar Inn, which is north-east of Varrock. If you bring the steel gauntlets to Johnathon (and they have already been imbued with another power) you must bring 25,000 coins to change them.

label: Chaos rune
title: Chaos rune
lead:
Chaos runes are used for low level missile spells, such as wind bolt, water bolt, earth bolt and fire bolt. They are also used to charge the bone staff, warped sceptre, trident of the seas, trident of the swamp, the eye of ayak, and Tumeken's shadow.

They spawn in the Wilderness near some moss giants, in the north-west corner of the Dark Warriors' Fortress, and can also be bought from the Varrock and Port Sarim magic shops.

label: Chaos talisman
title: Chaos talisman
lead:
The chaos talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Chaos Altar in the Wilderness just north-west of Edgeville. It can be combined with a tiara to make a chaos tiara for 42.5 Runecraft experience. This will make the talisman disappear, but the tiara will allow one-click entry to the Chaos Altar when worn. Both the tiara and the talisman allow players to craft chaos runes.

The chaos talisman is also a part of the rare drop table, therefore any monster with access to the rare drop table has a chance of either dropping this talisman or a nature talisman (with a couple of exceptions being able to drop both, such as fire giants and abyssal demons). Mid-level ironmen might find it easiest to get this by fighting Abyssal Leeches in the Abyssal Area using the Fairy Ring circles.

label: Chaos Temple (Asgarnia)
title: Chaos Temple (Asgarnia)
lead:
The Chaos Temple is a temple of Zamorak located north of Falador, north-west of Goblin Village. It can be approached from the south by following the wall separating Taverley from Falador, or from the north by crossing the Wilderness ditch. Alternatively, if one has completed the easy Falador Diary, they may access it using the tight-gap shortcut from Burthorpe.

The building has two levels: the hosting several monks of Zamorak (level 17 & 22), one wine of Zamorak on a table as well as an altar; the hosting a single monk of Zamorak (level 22), and one wine of Zamorak on the table (the requires a total level of 500 to access and wearing Zamorak monk robes or the vestment robes. Members skills may count for this total, even on free-to-play worlds).

label: Chaos Temple (hut)
title: Chaos Temple (hut)
lead:
The Chaos Temple is a structure in level 38 Wilderness, west of the Lava Maze. It contains a Chaos altar where players can recharge and train their Prayer using bones on the altar (other remains such as demonic ashes do not work). Free players may visit the temple, however only members may take advantage of the altar's benefits.

Praying at the Chaos altar inside is a requirement for the Easy Wilderness Diary.

label: Chaos Temple (Wilderness)
title: Chaos Temple (Wilderness)
lead:
