Optionally, at Cooking level 50+, players may then use a chocolate bar (which can be found in the Cooks' Guild) or chocolate dust on the cake to make a chocolate cake.

label: Uncooked curry
title: Uncooked curry
lead:
Uncooked curry is made by adding a potato and either cooked meat or cooked chicken to a bowl of water (in any order) to create uncooked stew, then adding either three curry leaves or one spice. The final product is the same regardless of which of the two types of meat is used.

At level 60 Cooking, it can be cooked to make curry, granting 280 experience. Burning it will produce burnt curry. The player stops burning curry at level 74 Cooking.

label: Uncooked meat pie
title: Uncooked meat pie
lead: An uncooked meat pie is made by adding cooked meat or cooked chicken to a pie shell. It can be cooked to make meat pie, or if unsuccessful, a Burnt pie.

label: Uncooked pizza
title: Uncooked pizza
lead: Uncooked pizza requires 35 Cooking to make and is obtained by using a pizza base with tomato and cheese. It can be cooked on a range (but not a fire) into a plain pizza, which gives 143 Cooking experience. Some toppings can then be added, see the pizza page for more details. It is possible to fail the cooking, which will result in a burnt pizza.

label: Uncooked stew
title: Uncooked stew
lead:
Uncooked stew is an inedible food made using the Cooking skill. It is created by adding a raw potato and either cooked meat or cooked chicken into a bowl of water; the product is the same regardless of which type of meat is used. The ingredients can be added in any order.

Adding a first ingredient creates an incomplete stew and adding the second ingredient creates the uncooked stew. It can then be cooked at level 25 Cooking to make stew, granting 117 experience. Alternatively, adding three curry leaves or one spice before cooking the stew produces an uncooked curry, which can be cooked at level 60 Cooking to make curry, granting 280 experience.

label: Uncut diamond
title: Uncut diamond
lead:
An uncut diamond is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a diamond, requiring 43 Crafting and yielding 107.5 experience.

Uncut diamonds can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

label: Uncut dragonstone
title: Uncut dragonstone
lead:
Uncut dragonstones are rare gems which can be cut into dragonstones, requiring 55 Crafting and granting 137.5 experience. They can be obtained from the crystal chest in Taverley, unlocked with a crystal key, along with other various items.

While uncut dragonstones are available from the gem shop within Mor Ul Rek for 1,500 Tokkul, they are not in stock unless sold by another player. Their cut counterparts are dropped very rarely by a wide variety of monsters.

label: Uncut emerald
title: Uncut emerald
lead:
An uncut emerald is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make an emerald, requiring 27 Crafting and yielding 67.5 experience.

Uncut emeralds can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

label: Uncut jade
title: Uncut jade
lead:
An uncut jade is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel at level 13 Crafting to make a jade, granting 20 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the jade, resulting in a crushed gem and 5 experience.

Uncut jades are found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing; or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. Jades can also be found while panning at the Digsite near the River Salve, or they may be stolen from H.A.M members via the Thieving skill.

label: Uncut opal
title: Uncut opal
lead:
An uncut opal is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make an opal, granting 15 Crafting experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the opal, resulting in a crushed gem and 3.8 experience. Opals are the lowest level gemstone and are worth very little.

Uncut opals are found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing; or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. Opals can also be found while panning at the Digsite near the River Salve, or they may be stolen from H.A.M members via the Thieving skill.

label: Uncut red topaz
title: Uncut red topaz
lead:
An uncut red topaz is a semi-precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel at level 16 Crafting to make a red topaz, granting 25 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the red topaz, resulting in a crushed gem and 6.3 experience.

Uncut red topaz is found mostly with the Mining skill, only by mining gem rocks which are located in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing, or by mining the shell of the Gemstone Crab. They can also be obtained by completing hard Gnome Restaurant deliveries, by stealing from Dorgesh-Kaan Rich Chests, by completing the Wise Old Man's tasks, or by salvaging merchant shipwrecks. In addition, there is a very rare chance to find one while searching certain scenery objects across Gielinor.

label: Uncut ruby
title: Uncut ruby
lead:
An uncut ruby is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a ruby, requiring 34 Crafting and yielding 85 experience.

Uncut rubies can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

label: Uncut sapphire
title: Uncut sapphire
lead:
An uncut sapphire is a precious gem used in Crafting. It can be cut with a chisel to make a sapphire, requiring 20 Crafting and yielding 50 experience.

Uncut sapphires can be obtained in several ways: randomly while mining ores, as drops from monsters (mainly those which have access to the rare drop table), gem shops, or as a reward from certain minigames and random events. They are also a common reward from Managing Miscellania.

label: Undead one
title: Undead one
lead:
The Undead ones play a critical part in the Shilo Village quest. Both skeletal and zombie undead ones are found in Ah Za Rhoon and Rashiliyia's Tomb, whereas the zombie undead ones are also found at the entrance to Shilo Village.

When the zombie variant is killed, they have the chance to release shilo mist that would damage the player for 2-3 Hitpoints per hit. However, it is not poisonous, so Antipoison is not required. The gas only affects characters in a one-square radius around where the undead one was when it was killed, so if players kill one, they have a few seconds to run to avoid taking damage.

label: Undead tree
title: Undead tree
lead:
Undead trees are located in the front yard of Draynor Manor and in the Haunted Woods. Unlike the dead trees surrounding them, they attack players walking past them for 0 to 3 melee damage. Undead trees maintain aggressiveness regardless of a player's combat level, and follow standard rules for tolerance. They can be spotted by their yellow examine option, identifying them as an NPC, and are also slightly smaller in size.

Undead trees cannot be cut until the Animal Magnetism quest, where the player obtains a blessed axe. Attempting to chop the tree with no axe results in the message You don't have an axe which could possibly affect this wood. Attempting to chop the tree with any axe other than the blessed axe will result in the message The axe bounces off the undead wood. and an animation of swinging the axe and it bouncing off the tree. It is also currently not possible to chop down the tree through intentional mechanics. 35 Woodcutting is required to cut the tree, having less results in the message You need a Woodcutting level of 35 or more in order to cut this tree. A Slayer level of 18 is required to chop the tree, having less results in the message

label: Undercurrent
title: Undercurrent
lead:
Undercurrent is a music track that can be unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays in the Wilderness between the Bandit Camp and the Graveyard of Shadows.

label: Underground (music track)
title: Underground (music track)
lead:
Underground is a music track that is unlocked in various locations around Gielinor:
*Wilderness
*Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon
*Entrana Dungeon
*Deepfin Mine
*Area of Taverley Dungeon containing Black Demons.

It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing the Tree spirit in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Underground Pass
title: Underground Pass
lead: Underground Pass is the third quest in the Elf quest series, and explores an extensive and perilous dungeon to the west of Ardougne. You must venture through the pass at the request of King Lathas, in order to help him destroy his corrupted brother Tyras.

label: Underground Pass (dungeon)
title: Underground Pass (dungeon)
lead: The Underground Pass is one of the pathways to reach Tirannwn, the elven lands of western Gielinor. Traversing the enormous and hostile dungeon is the focus of the eponymous Underground Pass quest.

label: Underground Pass (music track)
title: Underground Pass (music track)
lead: Underground Pass is a music track that is unlocked during the Underground Pass quest. It is unlocked in the second area of the Underground Pass, and in the pitfall trap underneath the grid in the first area.

label: Understanding
title: Understanding
lead:
Understanding is a music track that is unlocked at the Nature Altar.

This is only unlocked when entering the altar directly and is not unlocked through Guardians of the Rift.

label: Unfermented wine
title: Unfermented wine
lead:
An Unfermented wine is created when a player with a Cooking level of 35 or more uses grapes with a jug of water. After 12 seconds, this item will automatically turn to either a jug of wine, granting 200 Cooking experience, or a jug of bad wine, granting none. With 14 wines possible per inventory, each inventory grants you 2800 experience once fermented. The player will also stop making bad wine at level 68 Cooking.

Wine ferments on a single 12 second timer that resets each time the player makes a new jug of unfermented wine, whether banked or in their inventory. This means that any stack of wine in their bank will ferment all at once. Due to that, players can obtain massive amounts of experience in one tick.

label: Unfermented wine (unobtainable item)
title: Unfermented wine (unobtainable item)
lead:
Unfermented wine is an unobtainable version of Unfermented wine. Unfermented wines could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams where players conflated them with Half full wine jugs. Any player who had a noted unfermented wine was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real wine, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

label: Unferth
title: Unferth
lead:
Unferth is the human pet of Bob the Jagex cat. He is the starting point for the 'A Tail of Two Cats' quest, in which he asks the player to find his missing pet cat, Bob.

The Apothecary states that Unferth is a hypochondriac, and gets fed up every time he comes to him seeking a cure for his "illness".

label: Unfinished batta (cheese+tom, historical)
title: Unfinished batta (cheese+tom, historical)
lead:
An unfinished batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Cheese+tom batta. It could be made by adding Cheese and a Tomato to a Half baked batta, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to create a Cheese+tom batta. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd batta would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made batta, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished batta. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Cheese+tom batta.

label: Unfinished batta (fruit, historical)
title: Unfinished batta (fruit, historical)
lead:
An unfinished batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Fruit batta. It could be made by adding four equa leaves to a Half baked batta, then baking it. Players then could add lime chunks, orange chunks, and pineapple chunks in any order, before finally adding Gnome spice. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd batta would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made batta, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished batta. Once again, gnome spice is used to convert this into a Fruit batta.

label: Unfinished batta (vegetable, historical)
title: Unfinished batta (vegetable, historical)
lead:
An unfinished batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Vegetable batta. It could be made by adding two Tomatoes, an Onion, a Cabbage, some Dwellberries, and some Cheese to a Half baked batta, then baking it. Finally Equa leaves were added to make a Vegetable batta. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd batta would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made batta, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished batta. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Vegetable batta.

label: Unfinished batta (worm, historical)
title: Unfinished batta (worm, historical)
lead:
An unfinished batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Worm batta. It could be made by adding a Spicy worm and some cheese to a Half baked batta, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to make a Worm batta. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd batta would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made batta, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished batta. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Worm batta.

label: Unfinished bowl (chocolate bomb, historical)
title: Unfinished bowl (chocolate bomb, historical)
lead:
An unfinished bowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Chocolate bomb. It could be made by adding four Chocolate bars and some Equa leaves to a Half baked bowl, then baking it. The following items could then be added:
# A pot of cream to make the second unfinished bowl
# Another pot of cream to make the third unfinished bowl
# Some chocolate dust to complete the chocolate bomb
If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd gnomebowl would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made bowl, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished bowl. The chocolate and cream garnishes are now added at once.

label: Unfinished bowl (veg ball, historical)
title: Unfinished bowl (veg ball, historical)
lead:
An unfinished bowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Veg ball. It could be made by adding two Onions, two Potatos, and some Gnome spice to a Half baked bowl, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to make a veg ball. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd gnomebowl would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made bowl, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished bowl. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Veg ball.

label: Unfinished bowl (worm hole, historical)
title: Unfinished bowl (worm hole, historical)
lead:
An unfinished bowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Worm hole. It could be made by adding four King worms, two Onions, and some Gnome spice to a Half baked bowl, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to make a worm hole. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd gnomebowl would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made bowl, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished bowl. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Worm hole.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Blurberry special, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Blurberry special, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Blurberry special. It could be made by adding Vodka, Gin, Brandy, two Lemons, and an Orange to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass.
The following secondary items could then be added:
# Some orange chunks to make the second unfinished cocktail
# Some lemon chunks to make the third unfinished cocktail
# Some lime slices to make the fourth unfinished cocktail
# Some equa leaves to complete the Blurberry special
If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed special. The secondary ingredients are also automatically added at once by pouring the Mixed special into a cocktail glass.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Choc saturday, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Choc saturday, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Choc saturday. It could be made by adding Whisky, some Equa leaves and a Bucket of milk to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass.
The following secondary items could then be added:
# A chocolate bar to make the second unfinished cocktail
# Cooking it to make the third unfinished cocktail
# A pot of cream to make the fourth unfinished cocktail
# Some chocolate dust to complete the Choc saturday
If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed saturday (shaker). Unlike most other Gnome cuisine, this recipe still contains additional steps. Although the chocolate bar is now added automatically, the Mixed saturday must still be poured into a cocktail glass and cooked, with the pot of cream and chocolate dust added afterwards.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Drunk dragon, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Drunk dragon, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Drunk dragon. It could be made by adding Vodka, Gin, and some Dwellberries to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass.
The following secondary items could then be added:
# Some pineapple chunks to make the second unfinished cocktail
# A pot of cream to make the third unfinished cocktail
# Cooking it to complete the Drunk dragon
If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed dragon (shaker). Unlike most other Gnome cuisine, this recipe still contains additional steps. The Mixed dragon must still be poured into a cocktail glass, with the pineapple chunks and pot of cream being added next, and finally cooked.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Fruit blast, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Fruit blast, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Fruit blast. It could be made by adding a Pineapple, an Orange, and a Lemon to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass. Some Lemon slices could then be added to complete the Fruit blast. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed blast. The secondary ingredients are also automatically added at once by pouring the Mixed blast into a cocktail glass.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Pineapple punch, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Pineapple punch, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Pineapple punch. It could be made by adding two Pineapples, a Lemon and an Orange to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass.
The following secondary items could then be added:

If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed punch. The secondary ingredients are also automatically added at once by pouring the Mixed punch into a cocktail glass.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Short green guy, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Short green guy, historical)
lead:

The following secondary items could then be added:
# Some equa leaves to make the second unfinished cocktail

If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to the cocktail shaker to create a Mixed sgg. The secondary ingredients are also automatically added at once by pouring the Mixed sgg into a cocktail glass.

label: Unfinished cocktail (Wizard blizzard, historical)
title: Unfinished cocktail (Wizard blizzard, historical)
lead:
An unfinished cocktail was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Wizard blizzard. It could be made by adding two bottles of Vodka, some Gin, a Pineapple, an Orange, a Lime, and a Lemon to a Cocktail shaker, then pouring this into a Cocktail glass.
The following secondary items could then be added:
# Some pineapple chunks to make the second unfinished cocktail

If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd cocktail would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. The secondary ingredients are also automatically added at once by pouring the Mixed blizzard into a cocktail glass.

label: Unfinished crunchy (chocchip, historical)
title: Unfinished crunchy (chocchip, historical)
lead:
An unfinished crunchy was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making Chocchip crunchies. It could be made by adding two Chocolate bars and some Gnome spice to a Half baked crunchy, then baking it. Finally, Chocolate dust was added to make some Chocchip crunchies. If a mistake was made at any point, some Odd crunchies would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made crunchy, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished crunchy. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into some Chocchip crunchies.

label: Unfinished crunchy (spicy, historical)
title: Unfinished crunchy (spicy, historical)
lead:
An unfinished crunchy was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making Spicy crunchies. It could be made by adding three portions of Gnome spice and two Equa leaves to a Half baked crunchy, then baking it. Finally, some Gnome spice was added to make some Spicy crunchies. If a mistake was made at any point, some Odd crunchies would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made crunchy, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished crunchy. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into some Spicy crunchies.

label: Unfinished crunchy (toad, historical)
title: Unfinished crunchy (toad, historical)
lead:
An unfinished crunchy was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making Toad crunchies. It could be made by adding two Toad's legs and some Gnome spice to a Half baked crunchy, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to make some Toad crunchies. If a mistake was made at any point, some Odd crunchies would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made crunchy, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished crunchy. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into some Toad crunchies.

label: Unfinished crunchy (worm, historical)
title: Unfinished crunchy (worm, historical)
lead:
An unfinished crunchy was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making Worm crunchies. It could be made by adding two King worms, some Equa leaves, and some Gnome spice to a Half baked crunchy, then baking it. Finally, Gnome spice was added to make some Worm crunchies. If a mistake was made at any point, some Odd crunchies would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made crunchy, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished crunchy. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into some Worm crunchies.

label: Unfired bowl
title: Unfired bowl
lead:
An unfired bowl is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel which requires 8 Crafting and yields 18 Crafting experience. The unfired bowl can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a bowl, granting 15 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, the bowl can crack in the oven, destroying the bowl and granting no experience.

For the quest Dragon Slayer I, an unfired bowl is required as one of four items in order to obtain Thalzar's map piece from the Oracle on Ice Mountain.

label: Unfired pie dish
title: Unfired pie dish
lead: An unfired pie dish is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel, which requires level 7 Crafting and yields 15 Crafting experience. The unfired pie dish can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a pie dish, granting 10 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired pie dish can crack in the oven, destroying the pie dish and granting no experience.

label: Unfired pot
title: Unfired pot
lead: An unfired pot is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel, which requires level 1 Crafting and yields 6.3 Crafting experience. The unfired pot can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a pot, granting 6.3 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired pot can crack in the oven, destroying the pot and granting no experience.

label: Ungadulu
title: Ungadulu
lead:
Ungadulu is a shaman who is possessed by Nezikchened during the Legends' Quest. He has a combat level of 70, which becomes 169 when his demonic possession overcomes him. His height also increases by a bit when he changes into his demonic possessed form. Despite this, Ungadulu cannot be attacked with melee or ranged weapons; he will throw players out of the Octagram, hitting them for between 4 and 10 damage. However, players can manually cast combat spells on him both inside and outside the Octagram to damage and kill him without being thrown by his spell. Players may also use Dynamite(p) to damage and kill Ungadulu.

After the quest, Yommi tree seeds and Holy force cannot be obtained.

label: Unholy mould
title: Unholy mould
lead:
An unholy mould is a mould which is used to make silver bars into unpowered symbols using the Crafting skill. To do this, the player can use it on any furnace using the Crafting skill. Unholy moulds can be found by speaking to the Spirit of Scorpius at his grave after completion of the Observatory Quest.

It is also a rare drop from chaos druids and elder chaos druids after completion of the quest. Zombies in Tarn's Lair can also drop them, even if the quest hasn't been completed.

label: Unholy symbol
title: Unholy symbol
lead:
An unholy symbol is a silver symbol blessed to imbue it with the unholy power of Zamorak. Players can make unholy symbols by using the Crafting skill, with a Crafting level of 17. First, a player must use a silver bar with a furnace while they have an unholy mould in their inventory and must have one free inventory space. This will give the player an unstrung emblem and they will receive 50 Crafting experience. Next, the player must string the symbol with a ball of wool, giving the player 4 Crafting experience and making the item into an unpowered symbol.

Finally, the symbol must be blessed either by the Spirit of Scorpius at the Grave of Scorpius, north of the Observatory, or by using an unholy book or book of balance with it. To bless the symbol using one of the books, a player must have a Prayer level of 50 or higher, and blessing the symbol makes the player expend (\frac{1}{10} * CurrentPrayerPoints) + 2 amount of Prayer points. Once blessed, the unpowered symbol becomes an unholy symbol and gains stat bonuses.

label: unicorn
title: unicorn
lead:
Unicorns can be commonly found wandering around forested areas. On members servers, unicorns drop the unicorn horn, which are used in Herblore to make antipoisons. Unicorns are one of the oldest monsters in the game, having initially appeared during the beta of RuneScape Classic. They are also one of the most updated monsters, having received four graphical updates since their release.

They respawn slowly, at a rate of ~53 seconds. Due to the relative length of respawn compared to how quickly they can be killed, it is advisable to farm them in the Kourend Woodland while world hopping in between kills, or to kill unicows instead. They will retreat from combat at low health.

label: Unicorn (Underground Pass)
title: Unicorn (Underground Pass)
lead: The unicorn is found in a cage within the Underground Pass. During the Underground Pass quest, players must obtain its horn by pushing a boulder nearby to crush it, smashing the cage and brutally killing the unicorn.

label: Unicorn horn
title: Unicorn horn
lead: A unicorn horn is used to make a herblore ingredient that can be obtained as a drop from unicorns and black unicorns. It can be ground down to unicorn horn dust using a pestle and mortar. The dust can then be used as an ingredient in antipoison, super antipoison, and sanfew serum potions. It is also used alongside a cowhide to summon a Unicow in Creature Creation.

label: Unicorn horn (Underground Pass)
title: Unicorn horn (Underground Pass)
lead:
A unicorn horn is obtained by crushing a unicorn trapped in a cage during Underground Pass. When examined it indicates that this horn is withered, which distinguishes it from a standard unicorn horn dropped by a normal unicorn.

The player must first search the cage that contains the unicorn to obtain a piece of railing and then use the railing to lever a rock down onto the cage, crushing both the cage and the unicorn in the process. The player can then search the remains to obtain this horn. Later in the quest, the horn must be thrown down a well along with three paladin's badges.

label: Unicorn horn dust
title: Unicorn horn dust
lead:
Unicorn horn dust is a Herblore ingredient obtained by using a unicorn horn with a pestle and mortar or as a drop from cave bugs and cave crawlers. It can be used with a marrentill potion (unf) to make antipoison or with an irit potion (unf) to make superantipoison. It is also one of the ingredients required to turn super restores into Sanfew serums. One unicorn horn dust is used on the quest Ratcatchers.

Wesley in Nardah can crush unnoted or noted herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.

label: Unicorn's head
title: Unicorn's head
lead: Unicorn's head is a piece of scenery found on Tutorial Island, in the Taxidermist's house in Canifis, and in the Pirates' Hideout in the deep Wilderness.

label: Unknown Land
title: Unknown Land
lead:
Unknown Land is a music track that is unlocked around Draynor Village. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Start and Wander.

In Classic mode, the track plays in southern Draynor Village.

label: Unknown print
title: Unknown print
lead:
The unknown print is a quest item used in the Murder Mystery quest. It is lifted off of the murder weapon by using a pot of flour and a sheet of flypaper and can then be compared with similar prints lifted off of the suspects possessions in order to identify the murderer.

After the murderer is identified, the unknown print becomes the killer's print.

label: Unlocked Ogre chest
title: Unlocked Ogre chest
lead: The unlocked ogre chest is located in Rantz's cave and is searched during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. The chest becomes unlocked after the player pushes aside the rock keeping the Locked Ogre chest shut. During the quest, the player has to search the chest to obtain ogre bellows.

label: Unpowered orb
title: Unpowered orb
lead: An unpowered orb is an item used to make air orbs, water orbs, earth orbs, or fire orbs using the Magic skill.

label: unpowered symbol
title: unpowered symbol
lead:
An unpowered symbol is a symbol of Zamorak made by stringing an unstrung emblem with a ball of wool, requring 1 Crafting, yielding 4 Crafting experience.

It is made into an unholy symbol by using a completed Unholy book or Book of balance, requiring 50 Prayer, or talking to the Spirit of Scorpius after completion of the Observatory Quest which also requires claiming an unholy mould from him. He will not give the player an unholy mould if there is one already in their inventory.

label: Unstamped letter
title: Unstamped letter
lead: The unstamped letter is received from the Examiner by talking to her and choosing "Can I take an exam?" This item starts The Dig Site quest. It needs to be stamped by the Curator of the Varrock Museum, in order to continue on with the quest. If you lose this item you can get another by talking to an Examiner in the Digsite Exam Centre.

label: Unstrung emblem
title: Unstrung emblem
lead: Unstrung emblems can be used with a ball of wool to create an unpowered symbol. The Spirit of Scorpius in the Grave of Scorpius will bless an unpowered symbol, resulting in an unholy symbol, for players who have completed the Observatory Quest. Players with an Unholy book or a Book of balance and a Prayer level of at least 50 can bless their own unpowered symbols to create unholy symbols at a cost of 4 Prayer points each.

label: Unstrung symbol
title: Unstrung symbol
lead: Unstrung symbols can be made at 16 Crafting with a silver bar and a holy mould at a furnace, granting 50 crafting experience. It can be used with a ball of wool to create an unblessed symbol. This can then be taken to Brother Jered who will bless it at level 31 Prayer (including F2P), or it can be blessed at level 50 Prayer using a completed Holy book.

label: Unusual armour
title: Unusual armour
lead:
Unusual armour is a quest item found during the Watchtower quest. Players can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille, even after the quest is complete. It serves no purpose during the quest and is merely a red herring. It cannot be worn.

The armour has a similar appearance to the original version of goblin mail, although with different colours.

label: Upcoming
title: Upcoming
lead: Upcoming is a music track that is unlocked at the Necromancer Tower, or when crashing the balloon transport system.

label: Valaine
title: Valaine
lead:
Valaine is the owner of Valaine's Shop of Champions on the of the Champions' Guild.

She runs a general store, allowing players to sell anything to her. She sells blue capes, black full helms, black platelegs, and adamant platebodies. It is not recommended to sell items to her as she is far away from a bank.

label: Valaine's Shop of Champions.
title: Valaine's Shop of Champions.
lead:
Valaine's Shop of Champions is a shop located on the of the Champions' Guild. It is operated by Valaine.

Although the shop stocks armour, it functions similarly to a general store in that any tradeable item can be sold to the shop.

label: Vampyre Slayer
title: Vampyre Slayer
lead: Vampyre Slayer is a free-to-play quest that takes place in Draynor Village. The player is asked to slay the terrifying vampyre count Draynor terrorising the village that lives in a large mansion just north of Draynor, with the help of an experienced vampyre slayer.

label: Vannaka
title: Vannaka
lead:
Vannaka is a highly accomplished fighter who serves as the Combat Instructor on Tutorial Island and a Slayer master in Edgeville Dungeon. He claims to be the greatest swordsman alive, which is suggested by his combat level of 146 and his ability to carry both a steel two-handed sword and dragon square shield at the same time, a trait unattainable by players. According to the 14th Postbag from the Hedge, his Strength level is 112.

During the tutorial, he dismisses the player character's attempts at making idle conversation, and proceeds to teach them how Melee and Ranged combat work. He tasks the player with slaying a giant rat in close combat. Afterwards, he instructs the player to kill a second rat from outside of the enclosure using ranged attacks, a strategy colloquially known as safespotting.

label: Varrock
title: Varrock
lead:
Varrock (Jagex pronunciation: ) is the capital of the kingdom of Misthalin. It is one of the largest cities in Old School RuneScape, and the largest city available to free players. In addition to being popular due to its proximity to the Wilderness, the city hosts the massive Grand Exchange, through which players can trade any item they wish, and features in many of the quests throughout the game.

Varrock can be entered from all sides, and each entrance has non-aggressive level 21 guards surrounding it. The city is safe for all players, although care should be taken when coming from Lumbridge through the south entrance, as there are aggressive level 7 and 20 dark wizards.

label: Varrock chapel
title: Varrock chapel
lead:
The Varrock chapel is a four-story building found in the north-east part of Varrock, which represents the Varrock branch of the Church of Saradomin. It's implied that the church is falling apart; the church's priest, Father Lawrence, is an alcoholic, and his room on the is a mess. Elsie on the second floor describes the church as draughty; furthermore, the two church-goers Martina Scorsby and Jeremy Clerksin are asleep in the pews.

Like most churches, there is an altar inside which will restore Prayer points to full when prayed at. There is also a yew tree just outside the church.

label: Varrock east bank
title: Varrock east bank
lead:
The Varrock east bank, also known as Varrock east or the East Varrock bank, is a popular bank found south of the Varrock Museum.

The bank was once a very popular place to buy and sell items from other players before the introduction of the Grand Exchange. Some of the more common items that were sold here were rune essence and player killing goods such as food, lower levelled weapons and armour, runes, and potions.

label: Varrock General Store
title: Varrock General Store
lead:
The Varrock General Store is one of the most popular stores in the game. Located in the centre of Varrock, it is a general store that is fairly typical of other such similar stores found in the game.

This store used to be a major player trading centre, acting as a sort of flea market for players looking for bargains and other players simply wanting to unload surplus goods that they may have on hand. Due to its central location of a busy player centre for both F2P and member worlds, its proximity to two banks, and its general reputation as a centre of commerce, it served as a major point of player to player commerce for many years. Frequently players would also advertise requests for player to player trades to either buy or sell items without even using the store, but merely being there because of the large numbers of people that would often be there looking for bargains. On some worlds the trading would spill out onto the centre plaza, you would see players requesting trades spilling beyond even both banks in Varrock.

label: Varrock Museum
title: Varrock Museum
lead:
The Varrock Museum is dedicated to the history of Gielinor. It is located east of Varrock Palace, just south of the city's church.

Several activities can be found within this museum that award experience as well as kudos, which unlock a variety of rewards. For instance, players with at least 100 kudos will be able to start the Bone Voyage quest, which grants access to Fossil Island.

label: Varrock Palace
title: Varrock Palace
lead:
Varrock Palace is the official residence of the ruler of Misthalin as well as the nation's primary diplomatic and military centre. Located in central Varrock, it is the largest building in the city.

Since the Fourth Age, Varrock Palace has been a hub of economic, political, and social development within Misthalin. The palace currently houses King Roald III and his wife, Queen Ellamaria. As their full-time residence, it is equipped with kitchens, barracks, dining areas, a church, a large garden, troop housing areas, and other facilities.

label: Varrock Palace Library
title: Varrock Palace Library
lead:
The Varrock Palace Library is a moderately sized library found on the ground floor of the Varrock Palace on the north side and is overseen by Reldo. The player will frequently visit the library to consult with Reldo or pick out texts and documents on several topics relevant to various quests they engage in. Surok Magis will also be stationed here until the completion of What Lies Below.

Beside the table in the north-east alcove of the room is the Varrock Census that lists the citizens of Varrock and their profession.

label: Varrock Sewers
title: Varrock Sewers
lead:
The Varrock Sewers are a network of tunnels under the city of Varrock. It is a fairly large multi-combat underground area filled with low to mid-level monsters and is one of the largest dungeons in free-to-play.

A knife, slashing weapon or sharp-object (e.g. scimitar) is required to access certain parts of the sewer to cut a spider web (note: a throwing knife will not work).

label: Varrock Square
title: Varrock Square
lead:
Varrock Square is a square found directly south of Varrock Palace. It contains a large fountain with four statues on each side; the square's signature landmarks. Players teleporting to Varrock appear here, unless you have completed the medium Varrock Diary and changed your teleport to south of the Grand Exchange.

Varrock Square is one of the city's largest business centres, and as such hosts a number of shops and open-air stalls. Full stores such as the Varrock General Store, Thessalia's Fine Clothes, and Zaff's Superior Staves surround the square. Baraek's fur stall and Benny's newsstand, from which players can buy Varrock Herald newspapers, can be found in the north-east corner of the square while Eliza runs the Speedrunning Reward Shop in the south-east. Nevet runs the Events Reward Shop from a stall in the north-west corner of the square.

label: Varrock Swordshop
title: Varrock Swordshop
lead: The Varrock Swordshop is a shop in southern Varrock run by a Shop keeper. The shop can be found opposite the Blue Moon Inn. The shop sells daggers, swords, and longswords, all of which range from bronze to adamant. A list of all prices in the shop is located below. Players use the shop as a speedy way to purchase lower-level weapons, though this shop does not see much business as many players consider scimitars to be a better weapon choice.

label: Varrock Teleport
title: Varrock Teleport
lead:
Varrock Teleport is a teleport spell in the standard spellbook which teleports the player to Varrock's town square, near the fountain. This spell may be transferred to a piece of soft clay at a lectern in the Study of a player-owned house, creating a teleport tablet. The same runes are required, as well as the Magic level needed to cast the spell, and the Magic experience is gained at the time the tablet is created.

Casting this spell is a requirement for completing the Medium Varrock Diary. Completing it allows players to switch the location of the teleport to the Grand Exchange by right-clicking the spell and changing the destination. Changing the default location using the right-click Configure option will also change the default teleport when using the Varrock Portal.

label: Varrock west bank
title: Varrock west bank
lead:
The Varrock west bank, also known as Varrock west, West Varrock bank, or historically the Bank of Varrock, is a popular bank found just south of the Grand Exchange. Beyond its proximity to many shops, the bank also offers close access to a nearby anvil. There is a Deadman chest in the bank.

The Varrock west bank was the first bank in RuneScape. On release, it could only store coins. Prior to the Grand Exchange, the bank was also a common market location, similar to Falador Park. Today, the bank is the most popular free-to-play bank, and rares and Halloween items are still traded here in some worlds.

label: Vase (Digsite)
title: Vase (Digsite)
lead:
A vase can be found while digging in the Digsite at a level 1 dig or searching skeletons in the Uzer Mastaba. It has no use.

Although this item can be found at the Digsite, Terry Balando doesn't have any dialogue when showing it to him.

label: Veg ball
title: Veg ball
lead:
A vegetable ball is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade veg balls are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 150 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a vegetable ball via gnome cooking with 35 Cooking, yielding 175 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Vegetable batta
title: Vegetable batta
lead:
A vegetable batta is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 11 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade veg battas are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 120 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a vegetable batta via gnome cooking with 30 Cooking, yielding 156 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Velrak the explorer
title: Velrak the explorer
lead:
Velrak the explorer plays a small role in the Heroes' Quest and Scorpion Catcher quests as he is the one who gives the player a dusty key (assuming that players are not fishing for lava eels in the Lava Maze during Heroes' Quest and do not have access to the Legends' Guild to buy a dusty key during Scorpion Catcher). He can be found in the Black Knights' Base in Taverley Dungeon in a prison cell.

To obtain the dusty key, the Jailer outside of the cell must be killed. The Jailer will then drop a Jail key, which is used to unlock Velrak's cell. When Velrak is asked if there are any good places to explore, he will provide the dusty key. When giving the player a dusty key, the message states that he "reaches somewhere mysterious". This may be a reference to the mystery of players having invisible backpacks.

label: Venture
title: Venture
lead:
Venture is a music track that is unlocked at the Digsite. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Lullaby.

In Classic mode, the track only plays at the Exam Centre.

label: Venture 2
title: Venture 2
lead: Venture 2 is a music track that is unlocked in the Digsite Dungeon, and a small cave inhabited by Doug Deeping.

label: Veronica
title: Veronica
lead: Veronica is the fiancée of Ernest. They came upon Draynor Manor, and Ernest went in to ask for directions, as they were a little lost. However, he hadn't emerged after an hour, and she began to worry. She doesn't consider him to be particularly brave. She is found outside the Manor, north of Draynor Village and starts the Ernest the Chicken quest.

label: Vial
title: Vial
lead: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.

label: Vial (jangerberries and guam leaf)
title: Vial (jangerberries and guam leaf)
lead:
A Vial is made in the Watchtower quest by adding a jangerberries to an unfinished guam potion. After adding ground bat bones, it can be enchanted by the Watchtower Wizard to make a Magic ogre potion. Adding a guam to a vial of jangerberries instead will cause the potion to explode and deal 5 damage.

The mixture can be created after completing the quest; however, it has no further use.

label: Vial (jangerberries)
title: Vial (jangerberries)
lead:
A Vial is made in the Watchtower Quest by adding jangerberries to a vial of water.

Adding a guam leaf will cause the potion to explode, dealing 5 damage to the player, destroying the items, and printing the message You mixed the ingredients incorrectly and the mixture exploded.. The jangerberries must be added to an unfinished guam potion to create a vial containing the berry and herb mixture.

label: vial of water
title: vial of water
lead:
A vial of water is an item made by using a vial on a water source other than a well. It is mainly used for training Herblore.

Vials of water can be purchased from the general store in Ardougne, Shilo Village, Rellekka, Jiminua's Jungle Store, and from Jossik in the Lighthouse. It can also be purchased from the Nightmare Zone using 145 reward points. You may buy them in packs of 100, called a water-filled vial pack, which starts at 201 coins.

label: Vigroy
title: Vigroy
lead: Vigroy is the cart driver that transports you to northern Brimhaven after you complete the Shilo Village quest. He can be found west of the bank in Shilo Village. He runs one end of the Shilo Village cart system that transports players between Shilo Village and Brimhaven for a fee with the other end ran by his brother, Hajedy.

label: Village
title: Village
lead:
Village is a music track that is unlocked in Canifis, or by looking into a mystical mirror during Desert Treasure I.

In Classic mode, the track plays in a larger area around Canifis.

label: Vine (McGrubor's Wood)
title: Vine (McGrubor's Wood)
lead:
The Vine in McGrubor's Wood is used to obtain red vine worms which are used in the Fishing Contest, Fairytale I - Growing Pains, and Wanted! quests.

Using a spade near these vines will place the worms directly into the inventory.

label: Vision
title: Vision
lead:
Vision is a music track that is unlocked at the Wizards' Tower. It can also be unlocked very rarely in the Wizards' Tower basement.

Playing this song to Cecilia may be required for an Easy Clue step.

label: Viyeldi
title: Viyeldi
lead:
Viyeldi is a spirit encountered during the Legends' Quest, when Nezikchened - disguised as Echned Zekin - asks you to kill him. When you first enter the Viyeldi caves, he pretends to be a blue hat on the ground until picked up. Upon beginning a conversation with him, he informs you of a different path you could take in the quest. You can choose to carry out Nezikchened's request, and kill Viyeldi using the Dark dagger that Echned Zekin gives you at the source of the holy water spring, or you could listen to him, and kill the warriors for the fragments of the Heart crystal to progress.

Killing Viyeldi, while quicker, results in a more difficult final fight, as you will have to defeat the three warriors San Tojalon, Irvig Senay, and Ranalph Devere alongside Nezikchened in the fight. You can avoid this if you listen to Viyeldi and give the dagger to Ungadulu instead, and kill the warriors. Ungadulu will also give you a Holy force card to use against Nezikchened and weaken him in the next two fights.

label: Viyeldi caves
title: Viyeldi caves
lead:
The Viyeldi caves, named after their resident spirit Viyeldi, are the lower floor of a cave system located in the Kharazi Jungle in southern Karamja. They play a major role in Legends' Quest, of which partial completion is required for access to the caves.

The Viyeldi caves may be visited after the quest for the purpose of a master cryptic step. Additionally, barrels in the room just above the caves (containing the winch used to enter) can be smashed for a chance at random treasure, such as noted cooked sharks.

label: vodka
title: vodka
lead: Vodka is a clear spirit that can be obtained from Heckel Funch in the Gnome Stronghold, The Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach, Jossik in the Lighthouse, Atlazora's Rest in Outer Fortis, or The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis. There is also a chance of receiving a bottle during the King's Ransom quest.

label: Volencia moss
title: Volencia moss
lead:
Volencia moss is a herb which requires level 3 Herblore to clean, yielding 2.5 experience. It is used in the Jungle Potion quest as the fourth herb that the player brings Trufitus. Players can make volencia moss by cleaning the grimy volencia moss obtained by searching the grey rocks at the Karamja Jungle mine, north of Shilo Village. In order to be able to collect the herb, the player must first have started the Jungle Potion quest.

Volencia moss is one of the items that Malignius Mortifer may ask the player to give to the Nature Spirit during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

label: Voodoo Cult
title: Voodoo Cult
lead: Voodoo Cult is a music track that is unlocked at the lower level of Ah Za Rhoon. It can later be heard during Legends' Quest in the Viyeldi caves. It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing Nezikchened in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Voyage
title: Voyage
lead: Voyage is a music track that is unlocked at the top of Baxtorian Falls.

label: Vulnerability
title: Vulnerability
lead: Vulnerability is a level 66 Magic spell within the standard spellbook. When cast on an opponent, their Defence level is reduced by 10% (or 15% if the tome of water is also equipped). The spell gives 76 Magic experience per cast and requires 1 Soul, 5 Earth, and 5 Water runes to be cast. The spell can only be cast if their stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you cannot stack stat reduction with multiple spells in a row.

label: Wall (Crandor and Karamja Dungeon)
title: Wall (Crandor and Karamja Dungeon)
lead:
The wall is interactive scenery in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon, north of the deadly red spiders. It cannot be opened until Dragon Slayer I is partially completed after sailing to Crandor and then opening the wall from the northern side to Karamja, unlocking the wall permanently from both sides.

The wall will automatically unlock itself after completing Dragon Slayer I, even if the player did not open the wall from the Crandor side during the quest.

label: Wall Pipe
title: Wall Pipe
lead:
The Wall Pipes are located on the southern wall of one of the houses in Hemenster, and are used in the Fishing Contest quest. During the quest, the player must put a garlic in one of the pipes, to make the Sinister Stranger move to another location, making the best fishing spot available for the player to use.

Interestingly, these pipes can be interacted with from larger distances than most objects. From right beside the pipes, or 1 square away from the pipes, players will walk towards the pipe and a chat message of the player saying "Ewww - it's a smelly sewage pipe." is shown. When interacted from 2 squares away, a chat message "I can't reach that.' is given in the chat box. Searching the pipe from 3 or more squares away, but within 8 or fewer squares away, the chat box will instead read "Nothing interesting was found.". Searching it from any further distance from the pipe will cause the player to walk to within 8 spaces of the pipe before giving the latter message. This behaviour occurs both when searching the pipes, or using items on the pipes.

label: Wampum belt
title: Wampum belt
lead: A wampum belt is a quest item used in the Shilo Village quest. It is given to the player at the start of the quest by Mosol Rei outside the east entrance to Shilo Village. The player gives the belt to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village in order to find out more about the curse placed on Shilo Village.

label: Wander
title: Wander
lead:
Wander is a music track that is unlocked around Draynor Village. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Start and Unknown Land.

In Classic mode, the track plays at the Falador Farm.

label: War ship
title: War ship
lead:
The war ship is an untradeable holiday item obtained during birthday events. It cannot be equipped, nor be interacted with in the inventory.

It was originally found in Glough's house in RuneScape Classic, where it could be picked up by players but did not have a use. The item was discontinued in 2004 with the transition to RuneScape 2, making it extremely rare, although worthless as it could not be traded.

label: Wardrobe (skeleton, cobweb)
title: Wardrobe (skeleton, cobweb)
lead:
Wardrobes are interactive pieces of scenery that can be predominantly found in spooky places such as the Draynor Manor, the Slayer Tower, or the abodes of witches and necromancers.

The wardrobe features two large doors with a line of faded golden veneer painted around the edges, crowned by a decorative piece of carved panelling, with a cobweb attached to its top-right corner.

label: Warhammer (unobtainable item)
title: Warhammer (unobtainable item)
lead:
The warhammer is an unobtainable item released alongside RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It was presumably a leftover from development, created in order to test the implementation of the new warhammers in RuneScape 2.

label: Warrant
title: Warrant
lead:
The warrant is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is obtained from Bravek after giving him a hangover cure and telling him about the kidnapping.

The warrant is used to distract the mourner guard by the entrance to the plague house in the south-east corner of West Ardougne, granting the player access to search for Elena.

label: Warrior (Lost City)
title: Warrior (Lost City)
lead:
The Warrior in Lumbridge Swamp is part of a band of adventurers who are looking for the lost city of Zanaris. The rest of his group will not say anything about its mission, but the Warrior, being the dimmest, reveals the mission. The Warrior does not have a good reputation with his team after that.

The warrior and his three companions, an archer, a monk, and a wizard, can be found in the north-west part of the swamp.

label: Warrior (Thieving)
title: Warrior (Thieving)
lead:
Warriors are human soldiers in the employ of certain cities of Gielinor. They can be found patrolling the streets of East Ardougne, but also maintain a presence in the north-western wing of the Varrock Palace, as well as the outer walls of the Ardougne Castle. A group of four warriors can also be encountered on the outskirts of the city, in a camp just north-west of the castle.

In terms of level and stats, warriors are very similar to guards, yet their lack of drops means they are rarely fought. However, warriors are an infrequently used alternative to thieving from stalls at lower levels. They may be pickpocketed at level 25 Thieving, giving 18 coins and 26 Thieving experience, while hitting the player for 2 damage if they are caught in the act. Warriors that keep watch over the Ardougne Market are quite convenient to rob, as any damage they may deal in retaliation can be redressed by stealing from the Ardougne Baker's Stall instead.

label: Washing bowl
title: Washing bowl
lead: A washing bowl can be found on a bench in Filliman Tarlock's Nature Grotto, south of the Mort Myre Swamp. Hidden underneath it is a mirror required for the Nature Spirit quest. The bowl respawns almost instantly and serves no purpose in the quest after revealing the mirror.

label: Watch
title: Watch
lead:
A watch is an item for solving coordinate clues whilst on Treasure Trails. A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-west, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest). After talking to him, you have to receive the sextant from Murphy at Port Khazard in order for Brother Kojo to give you a watch at the Clock Tower.

Although not required for coordinate clues, a watch can be used with a sextant and a chart in the inventory to find the coordinates.

label: Watchman
title: Watchman
lead: Watchmen are guards located on the middle floor of the Watchtower on the north-western end of Yanille. They can be attacked and pickpocketed at level 65 Thieving. Thieving from them yields 60 coins and bread along with 137.5 experience. The route outside of walls requires going west from Nightmare Zone. From inside the walls, walk north and follow the northern wall and use the underwall tunnel, requiring 16 Agility, or climbing rocks, requiring 5 Agility, then walk west to the Watchtower. On the north side of the building, climb the trellis, requiring 18 Agility, to the middle floor of the Watchtower.

label: Watchman (random event)
title: Watchman (random event)
lead:
The watchman was a random event that appeared during Thieving, similar to other guardian events such as the rock golem. His level differed depending on the player's combat level. The Watchman would say "(Player's Name), you are under arrest!" before attacking. He was removed in a hidden update in August 2006 due to players' complaints about being killed too quickly when pickpocketing at a low hitpoint level and wearing no armour. As a result, he has never been present in Old School RuneScape.

Eventually, references to him were removed from the Knowledge Base between 2 November and 5 November 2006.

label: Watchtower
title: Watchtower
lead: Watchtower is a quest about the conflict between Yanille and the ogres of Gu'Tanoth. It involves the restoration of the city's Watchtower so that it may defend itself against an ogre attack.

label: Watchtower (building)
title: Watchtower (building)
lead: The Watchtower is a fortified defensive structure situated on the northern wall of Yanille. Its primary purpose is to defend the city from the ogres that inhabit the nearby Feldip Hills. After completion of its eponymous quest, it can be accessed directly by casting Watchtower Teleport.

label: Watchtower Teleport
title: Watchtower Teleport
lead:
Watchtower Teleport teleports the player to the top floor of the Watchtower, just north of Yanille. Unlocking the spell requires completion of the Watchtower quest to read the spell scroll given as a reward by the Watchtower Wizard.

Casting this spell is a requirement for completing the hard Ardougne Diary. Completing the hard Ardougne Diary grants the ability to teleport to the centre of Yanille by right-clicking the Watchtower teleport icon in the standard spellbook.

label: Watchtower Wizard
title: Watchtower Wizard
lead:
The Watchtower Wizard is the wizard who built a strange crystal-run machine defending Yanille from the nearby ogres. This wizard initiates the Watchtower Quest.

Should any duplicated or leftover quest items be used on him, he will confiscate the item.

label: Water Altar
title: Water Altar
lead:
The Water Altar is a runic altar upon which water runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 6 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 5 Runecraft is required to craft water runes.

Players may create a water tiara here by using either a water talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 30 Runecraft experience. An elemental tiara can also be created here by using an elemental talisman and gold tiara, granting 40 Runecraft experience.

label: Water battlestaff
title: Water battlestaff
lead:
The water battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 54 Crafting by combining a water orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic water staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic water staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

label: Water Blast
title: Water Blast
lead:
Water Blast is a water-based blast spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 47 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the strongest water spell available to free-to-play players.

label: Water Bolt
title: Water Bolt
lead: Water Bolt is a water-based bolt spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 23 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: water controls
title: water controls
lead: Two water controls are used in the Elemental Workshop I quest to let the water wheel spin. Players can turn them, making the flow indicators green.

label: water elemental
title: water elemental
lead:
Water elementals inhabit the area accessed during the Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II below Seers' Village. This monster can be helpful in training Herblore as it always drops a vial of water upon defeat, as well as an array of grimy herbs. It can be accessed during and after the quest.

Killing one is a requirement for an Easy Kandarin Diary task.

label: Water orb
title: Water orb
lead:
A water orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Water by using the Charge Water Orb spell, requiring 56 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 water runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 66 Magic experience.

The Water Obelisk is located on the island across from the shore of Catherby, getting there by climbing a ladder at the end of Taverley Dungeon by the black dragons. Accessing this section of the dungeon requires the dusty key or 70 agility.

label: Water Pool
title: Water Pool
lead:
The Water Pool containing pure water is located in the Kharazi Jungle, and is used to fill the gold bowl during the Legends' Quest. Filling the bowl requires the player to use a hollow reed on the pool, as the rocks makes it impossible to fill the bowl normally.

Using the look option on the pool results in the message: "A pretty babbling spring. The water bubbles with a strange effervescence." Using the investigate option on the pool results in the message: "The water's hard to reach with all these rocks around. There's a narrow gap, but you'll struggle to fit a container through it."

label: Water rune
title: Water rune
lead:
Water runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used to cast water-based combat spells in the standard spellbook, as well as many spells found in other spellbooks. The Confuse, Weaken, and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience, require water runes in conjunction with body and earth runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of water, provide infinite water runes while equipped.

Water runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.

label: Water Strike
title: Water Strike
lead: Water Strike is a water-based strike spell in the standard spellbook, available starting at level 5 Magic. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Water talisman
title: Water talisman
lead: A water talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player use the Water Altar. Use the talisman on the altar to get inside allowing one to create water runes at the altar. It is also used to make a water tiara if you have a tiara and a water talisman and use them on the altar, granting 30 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft mist runes at the Air Altar, steam runes at the Fire Altar, or mud runes at the Earth Altar. The water talisman is consumed in the process.

label: Water Wave
title: Water Wave
lead:
Water Wave is a water-based wave spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 65 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the second-strongest water spell in the game, with the strongest being Water Surge.

label: Water wheel (Elemental Workshop)
title: Water wheel (Elemental Workshop)
lead: The Water wheel is found in the elemental workshop near the water elementals. During the Elemental Workshop I quest, players should make it turn by operating the nearby water controls.

label: Water wheel (frame)
title: Water wheel (frame)
lead: Water wheels are located on the north side of the Elemental Workshop near the water elementals.

label: Waterfall (music track)
title: Waterfall (music track)
lead: Waterfall is a music track that is unlocked south of the Baxtorian Falls. It can also be heard in Glarial's Tomb. It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing the Moss Guardian in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Waterfall Dungeon
title: Waterfall Dungeon
lead: The Waterfall Dungeon is a set of connected caverns underneath the Baxtorian Falls. The dungeon can be accessed during and after the completion of the Waterfall Quest, and is an important destination in the quest.

label: Waterfall Quest
title: Waterfall Quest
lead: Waterfall Quest is an intermediate quest about a legendary treasure hidden somewhere in the Baxtorian Falls. The waterfall holds the history of the great elven King Baxtorian and his wife Glarial.

label: Waterfall rocks
title: Waterfall rocks
lead:
Waterfall rocks are a set of wet rocks found in the first cavern in Ah Za Rhoon, which the player enters during the Shilo Village quest. They play no role in the quest itself, but can be used to leave the cavern.

Choosing to "look-at" them reveals a precarious pathway, which leads through the waterfall ahead. Searching the rocks will give players the option to follow this path, taking them just east of the stepping stones shortcut found south of the temple.

label: Waterlily
title: Waterlily
lead: Waterlilies are non-interactive scenery that can be found in bodies of water across Gielinor.

label: Waterlogged
title: Waterlogged
lead:
Waterlogged is a music track that is unlocked in the Mort Myre Swamp.

It can later be heard while Temple Trekking, during the Bridge puzzle and the battle with the creature on the boat trip. The track also plays during Sins of the Father, when escorting Ivan Strom past the Bridge puzzle. In the Mort Myre Swamp area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Dead Quiet and Stagnant.

label: Waterpump (Falador)
title: Waterpump (Falador)
lead: A Waterpump is a water source found by the entrance of the Hairdresser in Falador. Using it to fill an empty bucket is a requirement for the easy Falador diary.

label: Waterpump (Morytania)
title: Waterpump (Morytania)
lead: A Waterpump is a water source found east of Fenkenstrain's Castle and outside an abandoned village west of the Barrows in Morytania.

label: Waterskin
title: Waterskin
lead:
A waterskin carries up to four servings of water, and provides protection against the desert heat effect in the Kharidian Desert. The amount of water will be noted by the waterskins name in parenthesis e.g. "Waterskin (4)" is a waterskin that is holding the maximum amount of water.

These can be bought from Shantay, in the Shantay Pass, south of Al Kharid. There are several ways to refill waterskins. In the table below, different methods of refilling are given, along with the amount of water doses are refilled by that method. Note that it is possible to decant water into other containers, for example using a vial of water on an empty bucket. Doing this before refilling the waterskin will quadruple the amount of water refilled in the skin.

label: Wave
title: Wave
lead:
Wave is the sixth listed emote. Upon use, the player waves their left hand. This gesture is often used as a greeting and farewell, but can also be used to catch one's attention.

This emote is already unlocked upon making an account.

label: Wayne
title: Wayne
lead:
Wayne is the owner of the chainmail specialty shop, Wayne's Chains. He may be found in his shop, located in southern Falador. Wayne's Chains sells all chainmail up to adamant. Despite his cheap prices, his shop is normally deserted.

During the 2021 Christmas event, it is revealed he has been trying to obtain sets of goblin mail in order to complete Goblin Diplomacy and become an adventurer, eventually hoping to join the Legends' Guild.

label: Wayne's Chains! - Chainmail specialist.
title: Wayne's Chains! - Chainmail specialist.
lead: Wayne's Chains is a shop owned by Wayne located in southern Falador. It is the only shop that specialises exclusively in chainbodies.

label: weaken
title: weaken
lead:
Weaken is a level 11 Magic spell. When cast on an opponent, their Strength is reduced by 5%. The spell gives experience whether it hits or misses, making it a popular way to gain experience cheaply. The spell can only be cast if the targets stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you can not stack stat reduction with multiple spells in a row.

The spell grants 21 Magic experience and requires three water, two earth, and one body runes to be cast.

label: Weapon poison
title: Weapon poison
lead:
Weapon poison is a potion made by using dragon scale dust on a kwuarm potion (unf), requiring 60 Herblore, yielding a weapon poison and 137.5 Herblore experience. It can be applied to all metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, javelins, darts, and throwing knives, most daggers, spears and hastae as well. Weapon poison can be removed from a weapon with a cleaning cloth.

A single vial of weapon poison can poison only 5 arrows, bolts, darts, or throwing knives. This makes poisoning a substantial amount of ammo quite costly.

label: Weapon poison (unobtainable item)
title: Weapon poison (unobtainable item)
lead:
Weapon poison is an unobtainable item that was intended to be released with the Ranging Guild, but for unknown reasons was cut before launch. Most likely, it would have been sold by the Weapon poison salesman, who was also not released. Since Weapon poison was relatively difficult to obtain at the time, it is possible the developers feared making it available in a store would cause the item to become too common.

It is referred to in the game files as "Display poison". This suggests that, similar to the Tea seller, the Weapon poison salesman would have owned a stall, and yelled at any player who attempted to take the display poison.

label: Weapon poison salesman
title: Weapon poison salesman
lead:
The Weapon poison salesman is an unreleased NPC who would have been located in the Ranging Guild. His name suggests that he would have sold Weapon poison to the player, that could be used on darts, throwing knives, and the new javelins.

An unobtainable item called "Display poison" exists, that aside from the different colour is identical to the real weapon poison. This suggests that, similar to the Tea seller, the Weapon poison salesman would have owned a stall, and yelled at any player who attempted to take the display poison.

label: Weapon store key
title: Weapon store key
lead:
The Weapon store key is an item used during the Shield of Arrav quest to access the Phoenix Gang's weapon storage room. In order to obtain it, you must either be in or have a partner in the Phoenix Gang who can get the key.

This item was previously named just "Key" until the Varrock update, when it was renamed to "Weapon store key", possibly to avoid confusion with other keys.

label: Weaponsmaster
title: Weaponsmaster
lead:
The Weaponsmaster is a member of the Phoenix Gang and plays a role during the Shield of Arrav quest. He is located upstairs in the southern alley of Varrock (south-west of Aubury's Rune Shop).

Players who are trying to get into the Black Arm Gang will have to kill him to be able to pick up the two required Phoenix crossbows. He will also attack members of the Black Arm Gang if they try to talk to him.

label: Weird Old Man
title: Weird Old Man
lead: The Weird Old Man is an insane man who can be found outside the northern entrance to the Kalphite Lair.

label: Well
title: Well
lead: A well is a common object found throughout Gielinor, and is used as a source of obtaining water by using an empty bucket or cup on them. They are marked on the map with a icon, although other sources of water share the same icon.

label: Well (Paladin badges)
title: Well (Paladin badges)
lead:
A well is located deep within the Underground Pass, where the player sacrifices three Paladin's badges and a unicorn horn to the well for access to the final chamber of the dungeon in the Underground Pass quest.

After the completion of the quest, Iban's staff or upgraded version can be recharged for free when used on the well, instead of paying the Dark Mage in West Ardougne.

label: Well (Paterdomus)
title: Well (Paterdomus)
lead:
A well found in the dungeon under Paterdomus Temple is used in a number of Morytania quests such as Priest in Peril and In Aid of the Myreque. In Priest in Peril you first obtain Murky water from the well for Drezel to bless in order to free him.
